title.zh: 卷二百〇一 志第一百五十四 刑法三
title.raw: 卷二百〇一 志第一百五十四 刑法三 Volume 201 Treatises 154: Punishment and Law 3

sentences.zh: 天下疑獄，讞有不能決，則下兩制與大臣若臺諫雜議，視其事之大小，無常法，而有司建請論駮者，亦時有焉。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm, in doubtful criminal cases where verdicts could not be decided, they were sent down for mixed deliberation by the Two Institutes, grand ministers, and the censors and remonstrators; according to the magnitude of the matter there was no fixed law, and there were also times when the responsible offices submitted proposals for debate and refutation.
translations.idiomatic: When a doubtful case anywhere in the empire could not be resolved, it was referred for joint discussion by the Two Institutes, senior ministers, and officials of the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau. The procedure depended on the scale of the case and followed no fixed rule; responsible agencies also sometimes submitted proposals for debate and rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，廣安軍 民安崇緒隸禁兵，訴繼母馮與父知逸離，今奪資產與己子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong reign, An Chongxu, a commoner of Guang'an Circuit who was registered among the palace guard troops, sued his stepmother Feng, [alleging] that she had separated from his father Zhiyi and now seized assets to give to her own son.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong era (988), An Chongxu, a Guang'an commoner enlisted in the palace guards, brought suit against his stepmother Lady Feng. He alleged that she had left his father Zhiyi and was now seizing family property for her own son.

sentences.zh: 大理當崇緒訟母，罪死。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review judged Chongxu for suing his mother; crime: death.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review ruled that Chongxu, for suing his mother, was liable to death.

sentences.zh: 太宗疑之，判大理張佖固執前斷，遂下臺省雜議。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong doubted it; Zhang Dian, acting chief of the Court of Judicial Review, stubbornly adhered to the previous judgment, so it was sent down for mixed deliberation by the Secretariat and Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had doubts. Zhang Dian, deputy chief of the Court of Judicial Review, insisted on the original ruling, so the case was sent for joint deliberation by the Secretariat and Censorate.

sentences.zh: 徐鉉議曰：「今第明其母馮嘗離，即須歸宗，否即崇緒準法處死。

translations.literal: Xu Xuan submitted an opinion, saying: "Now if we merely clarify that his mother Feng once left, then she must return to the lineage; otherwise Chongxu is to be punished by death according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan argued: "If it is established only that his mother Feng had indeed separated from the household, she must be restored to her original status; otherwise Chongxu should be executed as the law requires.

sentences.zh: 今詳案內不曾離異，其證有四。

translations.literal: Now upon detailed examination of the case, separation never occurred; there are four proofs of this.
translations.idiomatic: Upon close review, the record shows no separation—and there are four pieces of evidence to that effect.

sentences.zh: 况不孝之刑，教之大者，宜依刑部、大理寺斷。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the penalty for unfilial conduct is a matter of great importance in instruction; it is proper to follow the judgment of the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the punishment for unfilial conduct is among the weightiest lessons of the law. The ruling of the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review should be upheld."

sentences.zh: 右僕射李昉等四十三人議曰：「法寺定斷為不當。

translations.literal: The Right Grand Councilor Li Fang and forty-three others submitted an opinion: "The judicial court's fixed judgment is improper.
translations.idiomatic: Right Grand Councilor Li Fang and forty-three colleagues argued: "The judiciary's ruling is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 若以五母皆同，即阿蒲雖賤，乃崇緒親母，崇緒特以田業為馮強占，親母衣食不給，所以論訴。

translations.literal: If we hold that the five types of mother are all the same, then although A-Pu was of low status, she was Chongxu's birth mother; Chongxu specially because Feng forcibly seized the farmland, and his birth mother had insufficient food and clothing, therefore brought the suit.
translations.idiomatic: Even if all five categories of 'mother' are treated alike, A-Pu, though of humble station, was Chongxu's biological mother. He sued chiefly because Feng had seized the family lands by force, leaving his birth mother without food or clothing.

sentences.zh: 若從法寺斷死，則知逸何辜絕嗣，阿蒲何地托身？

translations.literal: If we follow the judicial court's judgment of death, then what offense did Zhiyi commit to be left without heirs, and where could A-Pu find support for her person?
translations.idiomatic: If the court's death sentence stands, what fault has Zhiyi committed to be cut off without heirs—and where is A-Pu to find refuge?

sentences.zh: 臣等議：田產並歸崇緒，馮合與蒲同居，供侍終身。

translations.literal: We your ministers submit: The farmland and property shall all return to Chongxu; Feng should live together with Pu, supplying and serving for life.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that all the land revert to Chongxu, that Feng live with A-Pu and provide for her for life.

sentences.zh: 如是，則子有父業可守，馮終身不至乏養。

translations.literal: If so, then the son has the father's estate to maintain, and Feng for her whole life will not reach the point of lacking support.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the son would retain his father's estate, and Feng would never lack support.

sentences.zh: 所犯並準赦原。」

translations.literal: The offenses committed are all to be pardoned according to the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: All offenses involved should be forgiven under the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 詔從昉等議，鉉、佖各奪奉一月。

translations.literal: An edict followed Fang and the others' opinion; Xu and Dian each had one month's salary withheld.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved Li Fang's proposal. Xu Xuan and Zhang Dian each had one month's stipend deducted.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年七月，詔：「謀殺已傷，按問欲舉，自首，從謀殺減二等論。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xining, an edict: "Where plotting murder has already caused injury, upon interrogation when about to be exposed, voluntary surrender—from plotting murder reduce two degrees in punishment."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xining 1 (1068), an edict declared: "When a plotted murder has already caused injury, and upon investigation the culprit is about to be exposed but surrenders voluntarily, the penalty for plotting murder is reduced by two degrees."

sentences.zh: 初，登州奏有婦阿云，母服中聘於韋，惡韋醜陋，謀殺不死。

translations.literal: Initially, Dengzhou memorialized that there was a woman A Yun, betrothed during her mother's mourning to Wei, who hated Wei's ugliness and plotted murder but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The case began when Dengzhou reported a woman named A Yun, betrothed during her mother's mourning period to a man named Wei. Finding Wei repulsive, she plotted to kill him but failed.

sentences.zh: 按問欲舉，自首。

translations.literal: Upon interrogation when about to be exposed, she surrendered voluntarily.
translations.idiomatic: When interrogation was about to expose her, she confessed voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 審刑院、大理寺論死，用違律為婚奏裁，敕貸其死。

translations.literal: The Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review sentenced death; for violating the statute on marriage they memorialized for imperial decision, and the edict commuted her death.
translations.idiomatic: The Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review sentenced her to death. Because the betrothal violated mourning regulations, they memorialized for imperial decision, and the emperor commuted the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 知登州許遵奏，引律「因犯殺傷而自首，得免所因之罪，仍從故殺傷法」，以謀為所因，當用按問欲舉條減二等。

translations.literal: Xu Zun, prefect of Dengzhou, memorialized, citing the statute: "One who surrenders voluntarily after an offense involving injury or killing is exempt from the crime that gave rise to it, and still follows the statute on deliberate injury or killing"—holding plotting as the underlying crime, the provision on interrogation when about to expose and surrender should apply with reduction of two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zun, prefect of Dengzhou, memorialized citing the statute: "One who confesses after an offense involving injury or killing is exempt from the underlying crime and is sentenced under the statute on deliberate injury or killing." He argued that plotting was the underlying offense and that the provision on confession upon imminent exposure should apply, reducing the penalty by two degrees.

sentences.zh: 刑部定如審刑、大理。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice fixed the penalty as the Court for Review of Penalties and Court of Judicial Review [had ruled].
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice upheld the ruling of the Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時遵方召判大理，御史臺劾遵，而遵不伏，請下兩制議。

translations.literal: At that time Zun had just been summoned to serve as acting chief of the Court of Judicial Review; the Censorate impeached Zun, but Zun would not submit; he requested submission to the Two Institutes for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Zun had just been summoned to serve as acting chief of the Court of Judicial Review. The Censorate impeached him, but he refused to yield and requested that the case be referred to the Two Institutes for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 乃令翰林學士司馬光、王安石同議，二人議不同，遂各為奏。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Hanlin Academicians Sima Guang and Wang Anshi to deliberate together; the two men's opinions differed, so each submitted a separate memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hanlin Academicians Sima Guang and Wang Anshi to deliberate jointly. Their opinions differed, and each submitted a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 光議是刑 部，安石議是遵，詔從安石所議。

translations.literal: Guang's opinion favored the Ministry of Justice; Anshi's opinion favored Zun; an edict followed Anshi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sided with the Ministry of Justice; Anshi sided with Xu Zun. An edict adopted Anshi's position.

sentences.zh: 而御史中丞滕甫猶請再選官定議，御史錢顗請罷遵大理，詔送翰林學士呂公著、韓維、知制誥錢公輔重定。

translations.literal: But Censor-in-Chief Teng Fu still requested selecting officials again to fix the decision; Censor Qian Yi requested removing Zun from the Court of Judicial Review; an edict sent it to Hanlin Academicians Lü Gongzhu, Han Wei, and Drafter Qian Gongfu to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Teng Fu nevertheless asked that new officials be appointed to settle the matter. Censor Qian Yi requested that Xu Zun be removed from the Court of Judicial Review. An edict referred the case to Hanlin Academicians Lü Gongzhu and Han Wei and Drafter Qian Gongfu for a new determination.

sentences.zh: 公著等議如安石，制曰「可」。

translations.literal: Gongzhu and the others' opinion agreed with Anshi; rescript said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongzhu and his colleagues agreed with Anshi. The rescript read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 於是法官齊恢、王師元、蔡冠卿等皆論奏公著等所議為不當。

translations.literal: At this the judicial officials Qi Hui, Wang Shiyuan, Cai Guanqing, and others all submitted memorials arguing that Gongzhu and the others' opinion was improper.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the judicial officials Qi Hui, Wang Shiyuan, Cai Guanqing, and others all memorialized that Lü Gongzhu's ruling was improper.

sentences.zh: 又詔安石與法官集議，反覆論難。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Anshi to deliberate collectively with the judicial officials, with repeated debate and refutation.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Anshi to confer with the judicial officials, and debate went back and forth at length.

sentences.zh: 明年二月庚子，詔：「今後謀殺人自首，並奏聽敕裁。」

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, day gengzi, an edict: "Hereafter in cases of plotting murder with voluntary surrender, all are to be memorialized for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, on the day gengzi, an edict declared: "Henceforth, all cases of plotted murder with voluntary confession shall be memorialized for imperial decision."

sentences.zh: 是月，除安石參知政事，於是奏以為：「律意，因犯殺傷而自首，得免所因之罪，仍從故殺傷法；

translations.literal: That month Anshi was appointed Vice Grand Councilor; thereupon he memorialized that the intent of the statute was: one who surrenders voluntarily after an offense involving injury or killing is exempt from the crime that gave rise to it, and still follows the statute on deliberate injury or killing;
translations.idiomatic: That month Anshi was appointed Vice Grand Councilor. He then memorialized that the intent of the statute was: "One who confesses after an offense involving injury or killing is exempt from the underlying crime and is sentenced under the statute on deliberate injury or killing;

sentences.zh: 若已殺，從故殺法，則為首者必死，不須奏裁；

translations.literal: if already killed, following the statute on deliberate killing, then the principal must die, and there is no need for memorialized decision;
translations.idiomatic: if the victim is already dead and the statute on deliberate killing applies, the principal offender must die and no memorial for imperial decision is needed;

sentences.zh: 為從者自有編敕奏裁之文，不須復立新制。」

translations.literal: for accomplices there is already text in the compiled statutes on memorialized decision, and there is no need to establish a new rule anew."
translations.idiomatic: for accomplices the compiled statutes already provide for memorialized imperial decision, and there is no need to create a new rule."

sentences.zh: 與唐介等數爭議帝前，卒從安石議。

translations.literal: With Tang Jie and several others he disputed repeatedly before the emperor, and in the end the emperor followed Anshi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He debated the matter repeatedly before the emperor with Tang Jie and others, and in the end the emperor adopted Anshi's view.

sentences.zh: 復詔：「自今並以去年七月詔書從事。」

translations.literal: Another edict: "Henceforth all are to follow the edict of the seventh month of last year."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered: "Henceforth all such cases shall follow the edict of the seventh month of last year."

sentences.zh: 判刑部劉述等又請中書、樞密院合議，中丞呂誨、御史劉琦、錢顗皆請如述奏，下之二府。

translations.literal: Liu Shu and others of the Ministry of Justice who fixed penalties again requested joint deliberation by the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs; Vice Censor-in-Chief Lü Hui, Censors Liu Qi and Qian Yi all requested as Shu memorialized; it was sent down to the Two Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu of the Ministry of Justice and others again requested joint deliberation by the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs. Vice Censor-in-Chief Lü Hui and Censors Liu Qi and Qian Yi all supported Liu Shu's request. The matter was referred to the Two Offices.

sentences.zh: 帝以為律文甚明，不須合議。

translations.literal: The emperor considered the statutory text very clear and that joint deliberation was unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the statutory text was perfectly clear and that joint deliberation was unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 而曾公亮等皆以博盡同異、厭塞言者為無傷，乃以眾議付樞密院。

translations.literal: But Zeng Gongliang and others all held that broadly covering all differences and silencing the speakers was harmless, so the collective opinion was handed to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang and others, however, thought it harmless to hear out every dissenting view and silence the critics, and the collective opinions were handed to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 文彥博以為：「殺傷者，欲殺而傷也，即已殺者不可首。」

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo held: "Injury or killing means intending to kill but only wounding; if already killed, one cannot surrender voluntarily."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo argued: "'Injury or killing' means intending to kill but only wounding. Once the victim is dead, voluntary confession does not apply."

sentences.zh: 呂公弼以為：「殺傷於律不可首。

translations.literal: Lü Gongbi held: "Injury or killing under the statute cannot be subject to voluntary surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongbi held: "Under the statute, injury or killing cannot be subject to voluntary confession.

sentences.zh: 請自今已殺傷依律，其從而加功自首，即奏裁。」

translations.literal: Request from now on where injury or killing has already occurred follow the statute; where accomplices added merit and surrendered voluntarily, then memorialize for decision."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that henceforth completed injury or killing follow the statute as written, while accomplices who added to the crime but confessed should be memorialized for imperial decision."

sentences.zh: 陳升之、韓絳議與安石略同。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi and Han Jiang's opinions were roughly the same as Anshi's.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi and Han Jiang took positions broadly similar to Anshi's.

sentences.zh: 會富弼入相，帝令弼議，而以疾病，久之弗議。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi entered as chief councilor, the emperor ordered Bi to deliberate, but because of illness, for a long time he did not deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi became chief councilor, the emperor ordered him to weigh in, but illness kept him from doing so for a long time.

sentences.zh: 至是乃決，而弼在告，不預也。

translations.literal: By this time it was decided, and Bi was on leave and did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: By the time a decision was reached, Fu Bi was on sick leave and took no part in it.

sentences.zh: 蘇州民張朝之從兄以槍戳死朝父，逃去，朝執而殺之。

translations.literal: A commoner of Suzhou, Zhang Chao's elder cousin by a different mother killed Chao's father with a spear and fled; Chao seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzhou, Zhang Chao's elder cousin killed Chao's father with a spear and fled. Chao captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 審刑、大理當朝十惡不睦罪死。

translations.literal: The Court for Review of Penalties and Court of Judicial Review judged Chao guilty of the Ten Abominations, crime of lack of harmony among kindred, death.
translations.idiomatic: The Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review sentenced Chao to death for the Ten Abominations, on the charge of lack of harmony among kin.

sentences.zh: 案既上，參知政事王安石言：「朝父為從兄所殺，而朝報殺之，罪止加役流，會赦，應原。」

translations.literal: The case having been submitted upward, Vice Grand Councilor Wang Anshi said: "Chao's father was killed by his cousin, and Chao repaid by killing him; the crime stops at increased labor service with exile, and encountering an amnesty he should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: After the case was submitted, Vice Grand Councilor Wang Anshi said: "Chao's father was killed by his cousin, and Chao killed the cousin in revenge. The offense warrants only penal servitude with increased labor and exile, and he should be pardoned under the amnesty."

sentences.zh: 帝從安石議，特釋朝不問。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Anshi's opinion and specially released Chao without prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Anshi's view and specially released Zhang Chao without further prosecution.

sentences.zh: 更命呂公著等定議刑名，議不稱安石意，乃自具奏。

translations.literal: He again ordered Lü Gongzhu and others to fix deliberation on penal names; the deliberation did not suit Anshi's intent, so he himself prepared a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Lü Gongzhu and others to deliberate on the penal designation. Their opinion did not satisfy Anshi, who then submitted his own memorial.

sentences.zh: 初，曾公亮以中書論正刑名為非，安石曰：「有司用刑不當，則審刑、大理當論正；

translations.literal: Initially, Zeng Gongliang held that the Secretariat deliberating and correcting penal names was improper; Anshi said: "When the responsible offices use punishment improperly, the Court for Review of Penalties and Court of Judicial Review should debate and correct;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zeng Gongliang had argued that it was improper for the Secretariat to debate and correct penal designations. Anshi replied: "When subordinate offices apply punishment incorrectly, the Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review should correct them;

sentences.zh: 審刑、大理用刑不當，即差官定議；

translations.literal: when the Court for Review of Penalties and Court of Judicial Review use punishment improperly, then dispatch officials to fix deliberation;
translations.idiomatic: when those courts err, officials should be dispatched to deliberate and settle the matter;

sentences.zh: 議既不當，即中書自宜論奏，取決人主。

translations.literal: when deliberation is improper, then the Secretariat itself should submit memorial and debate, taking decision from the sovereign ruler.
translations.idiomatic: when that deliberation is wrong, the Secretariat itself should memorialize and debate the issue, leaving the final decision to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 此所謂國體。

translations.literal: This is what is called the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant by the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 豈有中書不可論正刑名之理。」

translations.literal: How could there be principle that the Secretariat may not debate and correct penal names?"
translations.idiomatic: How could there be any principle by which the Secretariat may not debate and correct penal designations?"

sentences.zh: 三年，中書上刑名未安者五：其一，歲斷死刑幾二千人，比前代殊多。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Secretariat submitted five points where penal names were not settled: First, annual executions of the death penalty reach nearly two thousand persons, vastly more than previous dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Secretariat submitted five unresolved issues in penal law. First: nearly two thousand death sentences were handed down each year—far more than in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 如強劫盜並有死法，其間情狀輕重，有絕相遠者，使皆抵死，良亦可哀。

translations.literal: Such as armed robbery and banditry all having death statutes; among them circumstances of seriousness and lightness are utterly far apart; to make all pay with death is truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Armed robbery and banditry, for example, both carry the death penalty, yet the circumstances can differ enormously. To execute all offenders alike is truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 若為從情輕之人別立刑，如前代斬右趾之比，足以止惡而除害。

translations.literal: If for those whose circumstances as accomplices are light a separate penalty is established, like the former dynasties' cutting off the right foot, it would suffice to stop evil and remove harm.
translations.idiomatic: If a separate, lighter penalty were established for accomplices in minor cases—such as the former dynasties' punishment of cutting off the right foot—it would suffice to deter crime and remove harm.

sentences.zh: 禁軍非在邊防屯戍而逃者，亦可更寬首限，以收其勇力之効。

translations.literal: Palace guards who are not on frontier garrison duty but flee could also have the deadline for voluntary surrender widened, to harvest the effect of their courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards who desert while not on frontier garrison duty might also be given a wider window for voluntary surrender, so that their courage and strength could still be put to use.

sentences.zh: 其二，徒、流折杖之法，禁網加密，良民偶有抵冒，致傷肌體，為終身之辱；

translations.literal: Second, the statute on commuting exile and penal servitude to rod punishment—the net of prohibitions has grown denser; good commoners occasionally bump against it, causing injury to flesh, a disgrace for life;
translations.idiomatic: Second: the practice of commuting exile and penal servitude to flogging has tightened the net of prohibitions. Good citizens who occasionally transgress suffer bodily injury and lifelong disgrace;

sentences.zh: 愚頑之徒，雖一時創痛，而終無愧恥。

translations.literal: foolish obstinate fellows, though pained for a moment, in the end have no shame.
translations.idiomatic: while hardened offenders feel momentary pain but no lasting shame.

sentences.zh: 若使情理輕者復古居作之法，遇赦第減月日，使良善者知改過自新，凶頑者有所拘繫。

translations.literal: If for those whose circumstances are light the ancient method of living labor is restored, amnesty reducing months and days, good people would know to reform faults and renew themselves, and fierce fellows would have something to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: If lighter offenders were returned to the ancient practice of penal labor, with amnesties reducing their terms, the virtuous would learn to reform, and the vicious would be restrained.

sentences.zh: 其三，刺配之法二百餘條，其間情理輕者，亦可復古徒流移鄉之法，俟其再犯，然後決刺充軍。

translations.literal: Third, the statute on tattooing and assignment has over two hundred articles; among them those whose circumstances are light could also restore the ancient method of exile and penal servitude with transfer of domicile; wait until they offend again, then decide tattooing and assignment to military service.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the statutes on tattooing and military assignment contain over two hundred articles. For lighter cases, the ancient practice of exile or penal servitude with relocation could be restored; tattooing and assignment to the army would follow only upon a second offense.

sentences.zh: 其配隸並減就本處，或與近地。

translations.literal: Their assignment and registration should be reduced to stay in the original place, or to a nearby place.
translations.idiomatic: Assignments could be reduced so that offenders remain in their home region or a nearby area.

sentences.zh: 凶頑之徒，自從舊法。

translations.literal: Fierce obstinate fellows themselves follow the old law.
translations.idiomatic: Hardened offenders would still be subject to the existing law.

sentences.zh: 編管之人，亦迭送他所，量立役作時限，無得鉗。

translations.literal: Persons under registered supervision should also be sent in rotation to other places, with limits set on corvée labor term, not to be shackled.
translations.idiomatic: Those under registered supervision should likewise be rotated to other jurisdictions, with fixed terms of corvée labor and without shackling.

sentences.zh: 其四，令州縣考察士民，有能孝悌力田為眾所知者，給帖付身。

translations.literal: Fourth, order prefectures and counties to investigate gentry and commoners; those known by all for filial piety, fraternal duty, and tilling fields with strength—give them a certificate for the person.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: order prefectures and counties to identify local worthies known for filial piety, fraternal conduct, and diligent farming, and issue them personal certificates of merit.

sentences.zh: 偶有犯令，情輕可恕者，特議贖罰；

translations.literal: Those who occasionally violate orders, where circumstances are light and pardonable, specially deliberate ransom punishment;
translations.idiomatic: When such persons occasionally violate the law in minor, pardonable matters, special consideration should be given to commutation by fine;

sentences.zh: 其不悛者，科決。

translations.literal: those who do not reform, impose statutory penalty.
translations.idiomatic: those who do not reform should receive the statutory penalty.

sentences.zh: 其五，奏裁條目繁多，致淹刑禁，亦宜刪定。

translations.literal: Fifth, items requiring memorialized imperial decision are numerous, causing delay in penal prohibition; these also should be deleted and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: the many categories requiring memorialized imperial decision cause delays in the administration of justice and should be streamlined.

sentences.zh: 詔付編敕所詳議立法。

translations.literal: Edict: hand over to the Institute for Compiling Statutes for detailed deliberation and legislation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Institute for Compiling Statutes for detailed deliberation and legislation.

sentences.zh: 初，韓絳嘗請用肉刑，曾布復上議曰：「先王之制刑罰，未嘗不本於仁，然而有斷肢體、刻肌膚以至於殺戮，非得已也。

translations.literal: Initially, Han Jiang had once requested using corporal punishment; Zeng Bu again submitted a memorial saying: "The former kings in instituting punishments never failed to root them in benevolence, yet there was dismembering limbs, cutting flesh, up to slaughter—this was not their wish.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Jiang had proposed reviving corporal punishment. Zeng Bu submitted a further memorial: "The former kings, in establishing punishments, always rooted them in benevolence. Yet they dismembered limbs, cut flesh, and even took life—not because they wished to, but because they had no choice.

sentences.zh: 蓋人之有罪，贖刑不足以懲之，故不得已而加之以墨、劓、剕、宮、大辟，然審適輕重，則又有流宥之法。

translations.literal: For when people have guilt, monetary redemption punishment is insufficient to chastise them, so they had no choice but to add branding, nose-cutting, foot-cutting, castration, and great execution; yet examining suitability of heavy and light, there was again the method of exile and mitigation.
translations.idiomatic: When monetary penalties could not suffice to punish guilt, they had no choice but to add branding, nose-cutting, foot-amputation, castration, and capital execution—yet they also weighed severity and applied exile and mitigation where appropriate.

sentences.zh: 至漢文帝除肉刑而定笞箠之令，後世因之以為律。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Han abolished corporal punishment and fixed the order on flogging with bastinado, later generations took it as statute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Han abolished corporal punishment and established flogging with the bastinado, later generations adopted this as statute law.

sentences.zh: 大辟之次，處以流刑，代墨、劓、剕、宮，不惟非先王流宥之意，而又失輕重之差。

translations.literal: Next after great execution was exile punishment, replacing branding, nose-cutting, foot-cutting, and castration—not only contrary to the former kings' intent of exile and mitigation, but also losing the gradation of heavy and light.
translations.idiomatic: Exile was placed immediately below capital punishment, replacing branding, nose-cutting, foot-amputation, and castration. This not only departed from the ancient intent of exile as mitigation, but also erased the gradation between heavy and light penalties.

sentences.zh: 古者鄉田同井，人皆安土重遷。

translations.literal: In antiquity township fields shared wells; people all settled on the soil and valued migration.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity people shared communal fields by the well system; they were rooted to their native soil and loath to move.

sentences.zh: 流之遠方，無所資給，徒隸困辱，以至終身。

translations.literal: Exiling to distant regions, without means of support, bondservants suffered humiliation, even to the end of life.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to distant regions left offenders without support; as bondsmen they suffered humiliation for life.

sentences.zh: 近世之民，輕去鄉井，轉徙四方，固不為患，而居作一年，即聽附籍，比於古亦輕矣。

translations.literal: Commoners of recent times lightly leave their native hamlets, shift to all four directions, and it is truly not a worry; yet after one year of living labor they are permitted to attach to registers—compared with antiquity this is also light.
translations.idiomatic: People today readily leave their native hamlets and move in all directions, so exile is less burdensome; moreover, after one year of penal labor they may register locally—a lighter punishment than in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 况折杖之法，於古為鞭扑之刑，刑輕不能止惡，故犯法日益眾，其終必至於殺戮，是欲輕而反重也。

translations.literal: Moreover the method of commuting to rod punishment, in antiquity was the punishment of flogging; when punishment is light it cannot stop evil, so law-breaking daily grows numerous, and in the end must reach slaughter—this is wishing to lighten yet actually heavifying.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, commuting penalties to flogging—which in antiquity was a light punishment—cannot deter crime. Offenses multiply daily until they end in execution. The intent was to lighten punishment, but the result is to make it heavier.

sentences.zh: 今大辟之目至多，取其情可貸者，處之以肉刑，則人之獲生者必眾。

translations.literal: Now items of great execution are extremely many; take those whose circumstances can be spared, treat them with corporal punishment, then those who obtain life must be many.
translations.idiomatic: Capital offenses are now extremely numerous. If those whose circumstances warrant mercy were punished with corporal penalties instead, far more lives would be spared.

sentences.zh: 若軍士亡去應斬，賊盜贓滿應絞，則刖其足；

translations.literal: If soldiers desert and should be beheaded, or robbers whose booty is full should be strangled, then cut off their feet;
translations.idiomatic: Deserters who would be beheaded and robbers whose booty warrants strangulation would have their feet amputated;

sentences.zh: 犯良人於法應死，而情輕者處以宮刑 。

translations.literal: those who offend against good people and by law should die, but whose circumstances are light, treat with castration.
translations.idiomatic: offenders against law-abiding citizens who would otherwise face death but whose circumstances are mitigated would receive castration.

sentences.zh: 至於劓、墨，則用刺配之法。

translations.literal: As for nose-cutting and branding, use the method of tattooing and assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Nose-cutting and branding would be replaced by the existing practice of tattooing and military assignment.

sentences.zh: 降此而後為流、徒、杖、笞之罪，則制刑有差等矣。」

translations.literal: Below this are exile, penal servitude, cudgel, and bastinado crimes—then establishing punishment has gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Below these would come exile, penal servitude, cudgeling, and bastinado—thus restoring a graduated scale of punishments.

sentences.zh: 議既上，帝問可否於執政，王安石、馮京互有論辨，迄不果行。

translations.literal: The deliberation having been submitted, the emperor asked the chief administrators whether it was feasible; Wang Anshi and Feng Jing argued back and forth, and in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After the proposal was submitted, the emperor asked the chief administrators whether it was feasible. Wang Anshi and Feng Jing debated at length, and in the end the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博亦上言：「唐末、五代，用重典以救時弊，故法律之外，徒、流或加至於死。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo also submitted: "At the end of Tang and in the Five Dynasties, heavy codes were used to save the maladies of the time, so beyond the laws, exile sometimes was increased to death.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo also memorialized: "At the end of Tang and during the Five Dynasties, harsh codes were used to remedy the ills of the age. Beyond what the statutes prescribed, exile was sometimes increased to death.

sentences.zh: 國家承平百年，當用中典，然猶因循，有重於舊律者，若偽造官文書，律止流二千里，今斷從絞。

translations.literal: The state has enjoyed a century of peace and should use the moderate code, yet it still follows precedent; there are matters heavier than the old statutes—such as forging official documents, the statute only exile two thousand li, now judgment follows strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Our state has enjoyed a century of peace and should apply the moderate code, yet we still follow precedent in ways that exceed the old statutes. Forging official documents, for example, was punishable by exile for two thousand li under the statute, but is now punished by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 近凡偽造印記，再犯不至死者，亦從絞坐。

translations.literal: Recently, generally forging seals—repeat offenders not reaching death—also follow strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, repeat offenders in seal forgery who would not otherwise face death are also sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 夫持杖強盜，本法重於造印，今造印再犯者死，而強盜再犯贓不滿五匹者不死，則用刑甚異於律文矣。

translations.literal: Armed robbery with staff, the original statute is heavier than forging seals; now repeat forgers of seals die, while armed robbers who repeat but booty does not reach five bolts do not die—then use of punishment is very different from statutory text.
translations.idiomatic: Armed robbery with a weapon was originally a heavier offense than seal forgery under the statute. Yet repeat seal forgers are now executed, while repeat armed robbers whose booty falls short of five bolts are not—punishment has diverged sharply from the statutory text.

sentences.zh: 請檢詳刑名重於舊律者，以敕律參考，裁定其當。」

translations.literal: Request to examine penal names heavier than old statutes, using edicts and statutes for reference, fix what is appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: I request a review of all penal designations heavier than the old statutes, with edicts and statutes cross-referenced to determine what is appropriate."

sentences.zh: 詔送編敕所。

translations.literal: Edict: send to the Institute for Compiling Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Institute for Compiling Statutes.

sentences.zh: 又詔審刑院、大理寺議重贓併滿輕贓法。

translations.literal: Another edict: Court for Review of Penalties and Court of Judicial Review deliberate on the law of combining heavy booty to fill light booty.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered the Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review to deliberate on the law of combining heavier booty to satisfy lighter booty thresholds.

sentences.zh: 審刑院言：「所犯各異之贓，不待罪等而累併，則於律義難通，宜如故事。」

translations.literal: The Court for Review of Penalties argued: "Booty from different offenses should not be combined without regard to crime grades; this is hard to reconcile with statutory intent. Precedent should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: The Court for Review of Penalties argued: "Booty from different offenses should not be combined without regard to crime grades; this is hard to reconcile with statutory intent. Precedent should be followed."

sentences.zh: 而大理寺言：「律稱，以贓致罪，頻犯者並累科；

translations.literal: But the Court of Judicial Review said: "The statute states: one who causes crime through booty, frequently offending, combine and impose penalty;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review countered: "The statute states that one who repeatedly commits booty-related offenses shall have penalties imposed cumulatively;

sentences.zh: 若罪犯不等者，即以重贓併滿輕贓各倍論；

translations.literal: if crimes are not equal, then use heavy booty to combine and fill light booty, each multiplied in deliberation;
translations.idiomatic: when the crimes are unequal, heavier booty shall be combined to satisfy lighter booty thresholds, with each offense counted at double;

sentences.zh: 累併不加重者，止從重。

translations.literal: where accumulation and combination does not increase severity, only follow the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: where combination does not increase the penalty, only the heavier offense applies.

sentences.zh: 蓋律意以頻犯贓者，不可用二罪以上之法，故令累科；

translations.literal: The intent of the statute is that those who frequently offend through booty cannot use the method of more than two crimes, therefore order cumulative imposition;
translations.idiomatic: The intent is that repeat booty offenders cannot benefit from the rule against imposing more than two penalties, and therefore cumulative imposition is required;

sentences.zh: 為非一犯，故令倍論。

translations.literal: for not one offense, therefore order multiplication in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: because the offenses are not a single act, each is counted at double.

sentences.zh: 此從寬之一也。

translations.literal: This is the first leniency.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first lenient provision.

sentences.zh: 然六贓輕重不等，若犯二贓以上者，不可累輕以從重，故令併重以滿輕。

translations.literal: Yet the six booties heavy and light are not equal; if one offends in two booties or more, one cannot accumulate light to follow heavy, therefore order combining heavy to fill light.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the six categories of booty differ in severity. When two or more categories are involved, lighter booty cannot be accumulated to reach a heavier penalty; heavier booty must be combined to satisfy lighter thresholds.

sentences.zh: 此從寬之二也。

translations.literal: This is the second leniency.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second lenient provision.

sentences.zh: 若以重併輕後加重，則止從一重，蓋為進則改從於輕法，退亦不至於容姦。

translations.literal: If combining heavy with light later increases severity, then only follow one heavy—this is both advancing then changing to follow the lighter law, and retreating not reaching indulgence of vice.
translations.idiomatic: If combining heavier with lighter booty would increase the penalty beyond what a single heavy offense warrants, only the heavier penalty applies—ensuring that leniency when circumstances improve does not become indulgence of crime when they worsen.

sentences.zh: 而疏議假設之法，適皆罪等者，蓋一時命文耳。

translations.literal: But the commentary's hypothetical methods all happen to be equal crime grades—this was merely a temporary command text.
translations.idiomatic: The hypothetical examples in the statutory commentary, which happen to involve equal crime grades, were merely provisional formulations for instructional purposes.

sentences.zh: 若罪等者盡數累併，不等者止科一贓，則恐知法者足以為姦，不知者但繫臨時幸與不幸，非律之本意也。」

translations.literal: If crime grades are equal and all are accumulated in combination, but if unequal only one booty offense is charged, then perhaps those who know the law could enough to commit fraud, while those who do not know would depend only on temporary luck and misfortune—not the original intent of the statute.
translations.idiomatic: If equal crimes were always combined while unequal ones counted as a single booty offense, the law-wise could exploit the loophole while the ignorant would depend on chance. That would defeat the statute's purpose.

sentences.zh: 帝是大理議，行之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the Court of Judicial Review's opinion and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted the Court of Judicial Review's position and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 八年，洪州民有犯徒而斷杖者，其餘罪會恩免，官吏失出，當劾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Hongzhou had a case of a commoner who committed penal servitude but was sentenced to rod punishment; remaining crimes met amnesty and were pardoned, but officials erroneously released him and should be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, a Hongzhou man sentenced to penal servitude was wrongly punished by flogging instead. His remaining offenses were covered by an amnesty, but officials erroneously released him and should face impeachment.

sentences.zh: 中書堂後官劉袞駮議，以謂：「律因罪人以致罪，罪人遇恩者，準罪人原法。

translations.literal: A rear-office official of the Central Secretariat, Liu Gun, submitted a rebuttal, stating: "The law holds that when one causes another to incur guilt through a guilty person, and the guilty person receives grace, apply the original law of the guilty person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gun, a rear-office official of the Central Secretariat, submitted a rebuttal arguing that when guilt is incurred through a guilty person and that person receives an amnesty, the original penalty for the guilty person should govern.

sentences.zh: 洪州官吏當原。」

translations.literal: The officials of Hong Prefecture should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The officials of Hong Prefecture should be pardoned accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又請自今官司出入人罪，皆用此令。

translations.literal: He also requested that from now on, whenever offices wrongly convict or wrongly acquit persons of crimes, this statute should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that from then on, whenever an office wrongly convicted or wrongly acquitted someone, this rule should apply.

sentences.zh: 而審刑院、大理寺以謂：「失入人罪，乃官司誤致罪於人，難用此令。

translations.literal: But the Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review held that "wrongfully convicting a person of a crime is when an office mistakenly causes a person to incur guilt; it is difficult to apply this statute.
translations.idiomatic: The Court for Review of Penalties and the Court of Judicial Review objected that wrongful conviction occurs when an office mistakenly imposes guilt on someone, and that this statute could not readily apply in such cases.

sentences.zh: 其失出者，宜如袞議。」

translations.literal: As for wrongful acquittal, it is appropriate to follow Gun's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: Wrongful acquittal, they said, should follow Liu Gun's proposal.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，周清言；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, Zhou Qingyan:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng, Zhou Qingyan submitted the following:

sentences.zh: 「審刑院、刑部奏斷妻謀殺案問自首，變從故殺法，舉輕明重，斷入惡逆斬刑 。

translations.literal: "The Court for Review of Penalties and the Ministry of Justice adjudicated a case of a wife plotting murder and questioned voluntary surrender, changing to the statute on intentional killing, applying the principle of citing the lighter to clarify the heavier, and sentenced to the capital punishment of decapitation for rebellious regicide.
translations.idiomatic: The Court for Review of Penalties and the Ministry of Justice had ruled on a case in which a wife plotted murder and was questioned about voluntary surrender; they changed the charge to intentional killing, applied the principle of citing the lighter offense to clarify the heavier, and sentenced her to decapitation for rebellious regicide.

sentences.zh: 竊詳律意，妻謀殺夫，已殺，合入惡逆，以按問自首，變從故殺法，宜用妻毆夫死法定罪。

translations.literal: Upon close examination of the intent of the law, when a wife plots to kill her husband and has killed him, she properly falls under rebellious regicide; because of confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation, changing to the statute on intentional killing, it is appropriate to convict under the statute on a wife beating her husband to death.
translations.idiomatic: On careful reading of the law, a wife who plots to kill her husband and succeeds properly falls under rebellious regicide; but because the case turned on confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation and was shifted to the statute on intentional killing, conviction should follow the statute governing a wife who beats her husband to death.

sentences.zh: 且十惡條，謀與故鬥殺夫，方入惡逆，若謀而未殺，止當不睦。

translations.literal: Moreover, under the Ten Abominations, only plotting or intentionally fighting and killing the husband enters rebellious regicide; if one plots but has not killed, it should only be lack of harmony among kin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among the Ten Abominations, only plotting or intentionally fighting and killing one's husband counts as rebellious regicide; if the plot was not carried out, the offense is merely lack of harmony among kin.

sentences.zh: 既用舉輕明重，宜從謀而未殺法，依敕當決重杖處死，恐不可入惡逆斬刑。」

translations.literal: Since the principle of citing the lighter to clarify the heavier is used, it is appropriate to follow the law for plotting but not killing; according to the edict, one should be beaten heavily and executed, and I fear it cannot enter the capital punishment of decapitation for rebellious regicide."
translations.idiomatic: Since the lighter-to-clarify-heavier principle was invoked, the case should follow the rule for plotting without killing; under the edict that calls for heavy beating followed by execution—not decapitation for rebellious regicide.

sentences.zh: 下審刑院、刑部參詳，如清議。

translations.literal: The case was sent down to the Court for Review of Penalties and the Ministry of Justice for joint review, in accordance with Qing's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Court for Review of Penalties and the Ministry of Justice for joint review, and they followed Zhou Qingyan's opinion.

sentences.zh: 邵武軍奏讞，婦與人姦，謀殺其夫，已而夫醉歸，姦者自殺之。

translations.literal: Shaowu Circuit submitted a case for judgment: a woman committed adultery with another man and plotted to kill her husband; later the husband returned drunk, and the adulterer killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowu Circuit submitted a case for judgment: a woman had taken a lover and plotted to kill her husband; when her husband came home drunk, the lover killed him.

sentences.zh: 法寺當婦謀殺為從，而刑部郎中杜紘議婦罪應死。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review held the woman guilty of plotting murder as an accomplice, but Du Hong, Director of the Bureau in the Ministry of Justice, argued that the woman's offense warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review classified the woman as an accomplice in the plot to murder, but Du Hong, a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, argued that she deserved death.

sentences.zh: 又興元府奏讞，梁懷吉往視出妻之病，因寄粟，其子輒取食之，懷吉毆其子死。

translations.literal: Also, Xingyuan Prefecture submitted a case for judgment: Liang Huaiji went to visit his divorced wife's illness and left grain in deposit; her son promptly took and ate it, and Huaiji beat the son to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan Prefecture also submitted a case: Liang Huaiji visited his divorced wife, who was ill, and left grain with her; her son immediately took and ate it, and Huaiji beat the son to death.

sentences.zh: 法寺以盜粟論，而當懷吉雜犯死罪，引赦原。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review treated it as theft of grain, but held Huaiji guilty of a miscellaneous capital offense and invoked an amnesty to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review treated the grain as stolen property and found Huaiji guilty of a miscellaneous capital offense, then invoked an amnesty to pardon him.

sentences.zh: 而紘議出妻受寄粟，而其子輒費用，不入捕法。

translations.literal: But Hong argued that the divorced wife received grain on deposit, and her son promptly consumed it; this does not fall under the statute on apprehension.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong countered that the divorced wife had received the grain on deposit and her son had simply consumed it, so the case did not fall under the statute governing apprehension of thieves.

sentences.zh: 議既上，御史臺論紘議不當，詔罰金，仍展年磨勘。

translations.literal: After the opinions were submitted, the Censorate argued that Hong's opinion was improper; an edict imposed a fine and additionally delayed his merit review by one year.
translations.idiomatic: After these opinions were submitted, the Censorate held that Du Hong's view was wrong; the throne fined him and delayed his merit review by one year.

sentences.zh: 而侍郎崔台符以下三人無所可否，亦罰金。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Cui Taifu and three others below him neither affirmed nor denied, and were also fined.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Cui Taifu and three colleagues who had neither endorsed nor rejected the ruling were fined as well.

sentences.zh: 八年，尚書省言：「諸獲盜，有已經殺人，及元犯強姦、強盜貨命斷配之人，再犯捕獲，有司例用知人欲告、或按問自首減免法。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Department of State Affairs stated: "Of all captured robbers, there are those who have already killed people, and those originally guilty of rape or robbery who were commuted from death and sentenced to exile—when such persons are captured reoffending, the offices routinely apply the statutes on reduction for knowing that others intend to report, or confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the Department of State Affairs reported that when captured robbers who had already killed, or who had originally been guilty of rape or robbery and commuted from death to exile, were caught reoffending, offices routinely applied reductions for knowing that others intended to report the crime or for confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 且律文自首減等斷遣者，為其情非巨，有改過自新之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason the text of the law reduces rank in sentencing for voluntary surrender is that the circumstances are not grave and there is a mind to reform and renew oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The law reduces penalties for voluntary surrender only when the offense is not grave and the offender shows a genuine wish to reform.

sentences.zh: 至於姦、盜，與餘犯不同，難以例減。

translations.literal: As for adultery and robbery, they differ from other offenses and are difficult to reduce by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Adultery and robbery, however, are unlike other crimes and should not be reduced by analogy.

sentences.zh: 請強盜已殺人，?強姦或元犯強盜貸命，若持杖三人以上，知人欲告、按問欲舉而自首，及因人首告應減者，並不在減等例。」

translations.literal: We request that for robbers who have already killed people, or rape, or those originally guilty of robbery commuted from death—if three or more persons bearing weapons, knowing that others intend to report, confess upon imminent exposure under interrogation, or should be reduced because others reported first—they are all excluded from the precedent on reduction of rank.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that robbers who have already killed, or committed rape, or were originally guilty of robbery and commuted from death, as well as armed bands of three or more who surrender knowing others intend to report, confess upon imminent exposure under interrogation, or qualify for reduction because another informant came forward—all be excluded from reduction of penalty.

sentences.zh: 初，王安石與司馬光爭議按問自首法，卒從安石議。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Anshi and Sima Guang disputed the law on confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation, and in the end Wang Anshi's proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Anshi and Sima Guang had debated the law on confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation, and Wang Anshi's view had prevailed.

sentences.zh: 至是，光為相，復申前議改焉。

translations.literal: At this time, Guang was chief councilor and again raised his earlier proposal to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Guang had become chief councilor, he revived his earlier proposal to revise the law.

sentences.zh: 乃詔：「強盜按問欲舉自首者，不用減等。」

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "Robbers who confess upon imminent exposure under interrogation shall not receive reduction of rank."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Robbers who confess upon imminent exposure under interrogation shall receive no reduction of penalty."

sentences.zh: 既而給事中范純仁言：「熙寧按問欲舉條並得原減，以容姦太多，元豐八年，別立條制。

translations.literal: Later, Vice Director Fan Chunren stated: "Under the Xining statute on confession upon imminent exposure, all were eligible for pardon or reduction, which accommodated wrongdoing too broadly; in the eighth year of Yuanfeng, separate regulations were established.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Vice Director Fan Chunren argued that under the Xining rules on confession upon imminent exposure, offenders could all receive pardon or reduction—a latitude that sheltered too much wrongdoing—so in the eighth year of Yuanfeng separate regulations had been enacted.

sentences.zh: 竊詳已殺人、強姦，於法自不當首，不應更用按問減等。

translations.literal: Upon close examination, for those who have already killed or committed rape, the law itself does not permit voluntary surrender; reduction upon imminent exposure under interrogation should not be applied further.
translations.idiomatic: On careful review, those who have already killed or committed rape are not eligible for voluntary surrender under the law in the first place; they should not receive further reduction through confession upon imminent exposure.

sentences.zh: 至於貸命及持杖強盜，亦不減等，深為太重。

translations.literal: As for those commuted from death and armed robbers, not reducing rank is also deeply too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet denying any reduction to those commuted from death or to armed robbers is far too harsh.

sentences.zh: 按嘉祐編敕：『應犯罪之人，因疑被執，贓證未明，或徒黨就擒，未被指說，但詰問便承，皆從律按問欲舉首減之科。

translations.literal: According to the Jiayou compiled edicts: 'Persons who should be guilty of crime, because of suspicion are seized, evidence of stolen goods is not yet clear, or accomplices are captured but not yet identified, yet upon questioning immediately confess—all follow the statute on reduction for confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiayou compiled edicts provide: 'When a suspect is seized on suspicion, before stolen goods are proven or accomplices identified and named, if he confesses upon questioning, he receives the reduction accorded to confession upon imminent exposure under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 若已經詰問，隱拒本罪，不在首減之例。』

translations.literal: If already questioned and concealing or denying the original offense, he is not within the precedent on reduction for surrender.'
translations.idiomatic: If he has already been questioned and concealed or denied the original offense, he is not eligible for reduction on surrender.'

sentences.zh: 此敕當理，當時用之，天下號為刑平。

translations.literal: This edict is reasonable; when used at the time, the realm was called even in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That edict was sound; when it was in force, the realm was praised for even-handed justice.

sentences.zh: 請於法不首者，自不得原減，其餘取嘉祐編敕定斷，則用法當情，上以廣好生之德，下則無一夫不獲之 。」

translations.literal: We request that for those whom the law does not permit to surrender, pardon or reduction shall not be granted of itself; for the rest, judgment should be fixed according to the Jiayou compiled edicts—then the application of law will match the circumstances, above extending the virtue of cherishing life, below leaving no single man suffering wrongful conviction."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that where the law forbids surrender, no pardon or reduction be granted; for all other cases, judgment should follow the Jiayou compiled edicts—so that law matches circumstance, the throne's mercy toward life is broadened above, and below not a single innocent man suffers wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔；

translations.literal: An edict was also issued:
translations.idiomatic: Another edict was also issued:

sentences.zh: 「諸州鞫訊強盜，情理無可憫，刑名無疑慮，而輒奏請，許刑部舉駁，重行朝典，無得用例破條。」

translations.literal: "In all prefectures interrogating robbers, where circumstances afford no pity and the charge admits no doubt, yet they rashly submit memorials requesting imperial decision—the Ministry of Justice is permitted to cite rebuttal, impose heavy court discipline, and must not use precedent to break the statute."
translations.idiomatic: When prefectures interrogate robbers whose circumstances afford no pity and whose charges admit no doubt, yet rashly seek imperial decision, the Ministry of Justice may cite rebuttal, impose severe court discipline, and must not use precedent to override the statute.

sentences.zh: 從司馬光之請也。

translations.literal: This followed Sima Guang's request.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a petition from Sima Guang.

sentences.zh: 光又上言：「殺人不死，傷人不刑，堯、舜不能以致治。

translations.literal: Guang also submitted a statement: "If killers are not put to death and those who injure are not punished, even Yao and Shun could not achieve good order.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also memorialized: "If killers go unpunished and assailants unchastised, not even Yao and Shun could govern well.

sentences.zh: 刑部奏鈔兗、懷、耀三州之民有鬥殺者，皆當論死，乃妄作情理可憫奏裁，刑部即引舊例貸之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice submitted a memorial copy that among the people of Yan, Huai, and Yao prefectures who had fought and killed, all should be sentenced to death, yet they falsely made memorials on grounds of pitiable circumstances for imperial decision, and the Ministry of Justice immediately cited old precedent to commute them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice had circulated a memorial reporting that people in Yan, Huai, and Yao prefectures who fought and killed should all be sentenced to death, yet local offices falsely pleaded pitiable circumstances for imperial decision, and the Ministry immediately cited old precedent to commute their sentences.

sentences.zh: 凡律、令、敕、式或不盡載，則有司引例以決。

translations.literal: Whenever the code, statutes, edicts, or forms do not fully provide, then the offices cite precedent to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the code, statutes, edicts, and forms do not fully cover a case, offices cite precedent to decide it.

sentences.zh: 今鬥殺當死，自有正條，而刑部承例免死決配，是鬥殺條律無所用也。

translations.literal: Now fighting and killing warrant death and have their own proper article, yet the Ministry of Justice, following precedent, exempts from death and sentences to exile—then the article on fighting and killing in the code is useless.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting and killing carries a capital statute of its own, yet the Ministry of Justice, following precedent, spares offenders from death and exiles them instead—rendering the capital statute on fighting and killing meaningless.

sentences.zh: 請自今諸州所奏大辟，情理無可憫，刑名無可疑，令刑部還之，使依法處斷。

translations.literal: We request that from now on, for all capital cases submitted by prefectures where circumstances afford no pity and the charge admits no doubt, the Ministry of Justice return them and have them punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter, when prefectures submit capital cases whose circumstances afford no pity and whose charges admit no doubt, the Ministry of Justice return them for punishment strictly according to law.

sentences.zh: 若實有可憫、疑慮，即令刑部具其實於奏鈔，先擬處斷，門下省審覆。

translations.literal: If there are truly pitiable circumstances or doubts, then have the Ministry of Justice set forth the facts fully in the memorial copy, first propose the disposition, and the Gate Department review.
translations.idiomatic: If circumstances are truly pitiable or doubts genuinely remain, the Ministry should set forth the full facts in the memorial, propose a disposition in advance, and submit it to the Gate Department for review.

sentences.zh: 如或不當，及用例破條，即駁奏取旨勘之。」

translations.literal: If improper, or if precedent is used to break the statute, then cite rebuttal in memorial and seek the imperial decision for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: If the disposition is improper, or if precedent is used to break the statute, the Ministry should cite rebuttal and seek imperial direction for investigation."

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，純仁又言：「前歲四方奏讞，大辟凡二百六十四，死者止二十五人，所活垂及九分。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Chunren again stated: "In the previous year, memorials for judgment submitted from all quarters totaled two hundred sixty-four capital cases; only twenty-five were executed—the lives spared nearly reached nine tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou, Fan Chunren again reported: "The year before last, the four quarters submitted two hundred sixty-four capital cases for judgment; only twenty-five were executed—nearly nine tenths were spared.

sentences.zh: 自去年改法，至今未及百日，所奏按凡一百五十四，死者乃五十七人，所活纔及六分已上。

translations.literal: Since the law was changed last year, until now less than a hundred days have passed; submitted cases under interrogation total one hundred fifty-four, yet fifty-seven were executed—the lives spared barely exceed six tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Since the law was changed last year, fewer than a hundred days have passed; one hundred fifty-four capital cases have been submitted, yet fifty-seven were executed—barely more than six tenths spared.

sentences.zh: 臣固知未改法前全活數多，其間必有曲貸，然猶不失『罪疑惟輕』之仁；

translations.literal: Your subject knows well that before the law was changed the number fully spared was large, and among them there must have been improper leniency; yet it still did not depart from the humanity of 'when in doubt, favor the lighter'.
translations.idiomatic: I know that before the reform many more lives were spared, and some of that leniency was surely undue; yet it still honored the principle of 'when in doubt, favor the lighter.'

sentences.zh: 自改法後，所活數少，其間必有濫刑，則深虧『寧失不經』之義。

translations.literal: Since the law was changed, the number spared is small, and among them there must be excessive punishment—then it deeply violates the meaning of 'better to err by not executing'.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reform, far fewer lives have been spared, and excessive punishments have surely occurred—deeply violating the principle of 'better to err by sparing than by executing.'

sentences.zh: 請自今四方奏大辟按，並令刑部、大理寺再行審覆，略具所犯及元奏因依，令執政取旨裁斷，或所奏不當，亦原其罪。

translations.literal: We request that from now on, for all capital cases submitted from the four quarters, both the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review conduct further review, briefly setting forth the offense and the grounds of the original memorial, and have the chief ministers take imperial direction to decide; or if the submission was improper, also pardon the offense.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter all capital cases submitted from the four quarters be reviewed again by both the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review, with the offense and original grounds briefly stated, and that the chief ministers seek imperial direction to decide; if a submission was improper, the submitter's offense should also be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 如此則無濫之獄。」

translations.literal: Thus there will be no cases of excessive punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Thus excessive punishment would be avoided.

sentences.zh: 又因尚書省言，遠方奏讞，待報淹繫，始令川、廣、福建、荊南路罪人，情輕法重當奏斷者，申安撫或鈐轄司酌情決斷乃奏。

translations.literal: Also, because the Department of State Affairs reported that distant regions submitting cases for judgment waited so long for reply that prisoners were detained, it was first ordered that for criminals in Sichuan, Guang, Fujian, and Jingnan circuits, where the circumstances were light but the law heavy and imperial decision was required, they should first report to the pacification or military commission for discretionary judgment before submitting memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Department of State Affairs reported that distant circuits submitting cases for judgment were kept waiting so long that prisoners languished in detention, an order was first issued: in Sichuan, Guang, Fujian, and Jingnan circuits, when circumstances were light but the law heavy and imperial decision was required, the pacification or military commission might decide provisionally before submitting the memorial.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎韓維言：「天下奏按，必斷於大理，詳議於刑部，然後上之中書，決之人主。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Gate Department Han Wei stated: "Cases submitted from the realm must be finally decided by the Court of Judicial Review, closely deliberated by the Ministry of Justice, and then sent up to the Central Secretariat for the sovereign to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Gate Department Han Wei argued: "Capital cases from across the realm should be finally adjudicated by the Court of Judicial Review, closely deliberated by the Ministry of Justice, and only then sent to the Central Secretariat for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 近歲有司但因州郡所請，依違其言，即上中書，貼例取旨，故四方奏讞日多於前。

translations.literal: In recent years the offices, merely because prefectures requested, wavering in their words, immediately sent up to the Central Secretariat and attached precedent to seek imperial direction—hence memorials for judgment from the four quarters daily exceed those of former times.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, offices have merely echoed prefectural requests, wavering in their language, and immediately forwarded cases to the Central Secretariat with attached precedent seeking imperial direction—so submissions from the four quarters now exceed those of earlier days.

sentences.zh: 欲望刑清事省，難矣。

translations.literal: If one desires clear punishments and streamlined affairs, it is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Under such conditions, clear justice and streamlined administration are impossible.

sentences.zh: 自今大理寺受天下奏按，其有刑名疑慮、情理可憫，須具情法輕重條律，或指所斷之法，刑部詳審，次第上之。」

translations.literal: From now on, when the Court of Judicial Review receives submitted cases from the realm, if there are doubts in the charge or pitiable circumstances, they must set forth the articles on circumstances and law, light and heavy, or indicate the law under which judgment is rendered; the Ministry of Justice shall examine closely and submit in proper order."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when the Court of Judicial Review receives capital submissions from the realm, any case involving doubtful charges or pitiable circumstances must include the relevant articles on circumstances and penalty, or identify the statute applied; the Ministry of Justice shall examine closely and submit in proper order.

sentences.zh: 詔刑部立法以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to draft legislation and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to draft legislation and report back.

sentences.zh: 崇寧五年，詔：「民以罪麗法，情有重輕，則法有增損。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning, an edict stated: "When the people by offense touch the law, if circumstances have degrees of severity, then the law has increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongning, an edict declared: "When offenders touch the law, the gravity of circumstance warrants increase or decrease of penalty.

sentences.zh: 故情重法輕，情輕法重，舊有取旨之令。

translations.literal: Therefore when circumstances are heavy and the law light, or circumstances light and the law heavy, there was formerly an order to seek imperial direction.
translations.idiomatic: Where circumstances are heavy but the law light, or circumstances light but the law heavy, the old rule required seeking imperial direction.

sentences.zh: 今有司惟情重法輕則請加罪，而法重情輕則不奏減，是樂於罪人，而難於用恕，非所以為欽恤也。

translations.literal: Now the offices only when circumstances are heavy and the law light request increased punishment, but when the law is heavy and circumstances light do not submit for reduction—this delights in punishing offenders and makes mercy difficult; it is not how reverent compassion should be exercised.
translations.idiomatic: Now offices seek increased punishment when circumstances are heavy and the law light, but refuse to submit for reduction when the law is heavy and circumstances light—delighting in condemnation while shunning mercy, contrary to reverent compassion.

sentences.zh: 自今宜遵舊法取旨，使情法輕重各適其中，否則以違制論。」

translations.literal: From now on it is appropriate to follow the old law and seek imperial direction, so that circumstances and law, light and heavy, each reach the mean; otherwise treat as violation of edict."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter offices shall follow the old law and seek imperial direction, so that circumstance and penalty each reach their proper balance; otherwise they shall be charged with violation of edict.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，臣僚言：「元豐舊法，有情輕法重，情重法輕，若入大辟，刑名疑慮，並許奏裁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe, officials stated: "Under the old Yuanfeng law, where circumstances were light and the law heavy, or circumstances heavy and the law light, if entering capital punishment with doubts in the charge, all were permitted to submit for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xuanhe, officials reported: "Under the old Yuanfeng law, when circumstances were light but the law heavy, or circumstances heavy but the law light, capital cases with doubtful charges could all be submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 比來諸路以大辟疑獄決于朝廷者，大理寺類以『不當』劾之。

translations.literal: Recently, for doubtful capital cases from the circuits decided at court, the Court of Judicial Review routinely impeaches them as 'improper'.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, however, when circuits sent doubtful capital cases to court for decision, the Court of Judicial Review routinely impeached them as improper.

sentences.zh: 夫情理巨，罪狀明白，奏裁以幸寬貸，固在所戒；

translations.literal: When circumstances are grave and the facts of guilt are clear, submitting for imperial decision to seek leniency is indeed what should be guarded against;
translations.idiomatic: Seeking imperial decision to obtain leniency when circumstances are grave and guilt is clear is indeed to be guarded against;

sentences.zh: 然有疑而難決者，一切劾之，則官吏莫不便文自營。

translations.literal: yet when there are doubts and difficulty in decision, impeaching all alike, then officials will all conveniently use empty words for their own advantage.
translations.idiomatic: but when genuine doubts make a case hard to decide, impeaching every such submission will only encourage officials to hide behind empty formalities for private gain.

sentences.zh: 臣恐天下無復以疑獄奏矣。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that under Heaven there will no longer be doubtful cases submitted.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that under Heaven no doubtful case will ever be submitted again.

sentences.zh: 願詔大理寺並依元豐法。」

translations.literal: We wish an edict that the Court of Judicial Review follow the Yuanfeng law throughout."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Court of Judicial Review be ordered to follow the Yuanfeng law throughout.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，州縣盜起，道不通，詔應奏裁者，權減降斷遣以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, bandits arose in prefectures and counties and roads were impassable; an edict ordered that those requiring imperial decision might provisionally reduce and lower sentences and report.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era, banditry spread through prefectures and counties and roads became impassable; an edict permitted cases requiring imperial decision to be provisionally reduced and reported.

sentences.zh: 既而奏讞者多得輕貸，官無失入之虞，而吏有鬻獄之利，往往不應奏者，率奏之。

translations.literal: Later, those submitting cases for judgment mostly received lenient commutation; officials had no fear of wrongful conviction, while clerks profited from selling justice—often cases that should not have been submitted were all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon those submitting cases for judgment mostly received lenient commutation; officials faced no risk of wrongful conviction, while clerks profited from selling justice—so cases that should not have been submitted were submitted anyway.

sentences.zh: 三年，乃詔大辟應奏者，提刑司具因依繳奏。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict was then issued that for capital cases requiring submission, the judicial intendant should compile the grounds and submit the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict required that for capital cases requiring submission, the judicial intendant compile the grounds and submit the memorial.

sentences.zh: 宣州民葉全二盜檀偕窖錢，偕令佃人阮授、阮捷殺全二等五人，棄屍水中，有司以「屍不經驗」奏。

translations.literal: Ye Quan'er, a commoner of Xuan Prefecture, stole Zhan Xie's stored money; Xie had tenant farmers Ruan Shou and Ruan Jie kill Quan'er and four others, and abandoned the bodies in the water; the office submitted on grounds of 'bodies not examined'.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Quan'er, a commoner of Xuan Prefecture, stole money from Zhan Xie's storehouse; Xie had tenant farmers Ruan Shou and Ruan Jie kill Quan'er and four others and dump the bodies in the water; local officials submitted the case on the ground that the bodies had not been examined.

sentences.zh: 侍御史辛炳言偕係故殺，眾證分明，以近降法，不應奏。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Xin Bing stated that Xie was guilty of intentional killing, with numerous witnesses clear; under the recent lowered law, submission was not appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Xin Bing argued that Xie was guilty of intentional killing with clear testimony from many witnesses; under the recent lowered law, the case should not have been submitted.

sentences.zh: 諸獄不當奏而奏者雖不論罪，今宣州觀望，欲併罪之。

translations.literal: For cases improperly submitted though submission was not appropriate, though not punished by law, now Xuan Prefecture hesitates and wishes to punish additionally.
translations.idiomatic: Although the law does not punish improper submission, Xuan Prefecture now hesitates and seeks to impose additional penalties.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若宣州加罪，則實有疑者亦不復奏陳矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If Xuan Prefecture adds punishment, then those with genuine doubts will also no longer submit memorials."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If Xuan Prefecture adds punishment, then officials with genuine doubts will also cease to submit cases.

sentences.zh: 於是法寺、 刑部止罰金。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Court of Judicial Review and the Ministry of Justice only imposed fines.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review and the Ministry of Justice therefore imposed fines only.

sentences.zh: 五年，給事中陳與義奏有司多妄奏出入人罪，帝為申嚴立法，終不悛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Vice Director Chen Yuyi memorialized that the offices frequently submitted false memorials wrongly convicting or acquitting persons of crimes; the emperor issued strict legislation on their behalf, yet they never repented.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Vice Director Chen Yuyi reported that offices frequently submitted false memorials wrongly convicting or acquitting offenders; the emperor issued strict legislation in response, yet they never mended their ways.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，右正言凌哲復上疏曰：「漢高入關，悉除秦法，與民約法三章耳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Right Remonstrator Ling Zhe again submitted a memorial, saying: "When the High Ancestor of Han entered the passes, he abolished all Qin law and made only a three-article covenant with the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, Right Remonstrator Ling Zhe memorialized again: "When the Founding Emperor of Han entered the passes, he abolished Qin law entirely and bound the people to only three articles.

sentences.zh: 所謂殺人者死，實居其首。

translations.literal: What is called 'killers die' truly stands at the head.
translations.idiomatic: The rule that he who kills shall die stood first among them.

sentences.zh: 司馬光有言：『殺人者不死，雖堯、舜不能以致治。』

translations.literal: Sima Guang had a saying: 'If killers are not put to death, even Yao and Shun cannot achieve good order.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said: 'If killers are not put to death, not even Yao and Shun can achieve good order.'

sentences.zh: 斯言可謂至當矣。

translations.literal: This saying can be called utterly correct.
translations.idiomatic: Those words could not be more apt.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見諸路州、軍大辟，雖刑法相當者，類以可憫奏裁。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that among capital cases in prefectures and military commands of the circuits, even where punishment matched the law, they routinely submitted for imperial decision on grounds of pity.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that in capital cases across the circuits, even where law and circumstance clearly matched, offices routinely pleaded pitiable circumstances for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 自去歲郊後距今，大辟奏裁者五十餘人中，有實犯故殺、鬥殺常赦所不原者，法既無疑，情無可憫，刑、寺並皆奏裁貸減。

translations.literal: From the suburban sacrifice last year until now, among more than fifty submitted for imperial decision on capital punishment, there were those who truly committed intentional killing or fighting and killing not pardoned by ordinary amnesty; the law admitted no doubt and circumstances afforded no pity—yet both the Ministry of Justice and the Court submitted for imperial decision to commute and reduce.
translations.idiomatic: Since last year's suburban sacrifice, among more than fifty capital cases submitted for imperial decision, some involved intentional killing or fighting and killing excluded from ordinary amnesty—charges beyond doubt, circumstances beyond pity—yet both the Ministry of Justice and the Court submitted them for commutation and reduction.

sentences.zh: 彼殺人者可謂幸矣，被殺者銜恨九原，何時已邪？

translations.literal: Those who killed can be called fortunate; those killed harbor resentment in the nine springs—when will it ever end?
translations.idiomatic: The killers were fortunate indeed; the slain carry their grievance to the grave—when will that end?

sentences.zh: 臣恐強暴之風滋長，良善之人，莫能自保，其於刑政，為害非細。

translations.literal: Your subject fears the wind of violence will grow daily; good and honest people will be unable to protect themselves—for criminal administration the harm is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: I fear violence will flourish, and the law-abiding will no longer be able to protect themselves—a grave injury to the administration of justice.

sentences.zh: 應今後大辟，情法相當、無可憫者，所司輒奏裁減貸者，乞令臺臣彈劾。」
