translations.literal: For capital cases hereafter where circumstances and law match and there is nothing pitiable, if the office rashly submits for imperial decision to reduce or commute, we beg that censorial officials be ordered to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when circumstances and law match and nothing is pitiable, yet an office rashly seeks imperial decision to reduce or commute a capital sentence, I ask that censorial officials be empowered to impeach.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏曰：「但恐諸路滅裂，實有情理可憫之人，一例不奏，有失欽恤之意。」

translations.literal: The emperor, reading the memorial, said: "But I fear the circuits will be negligent, and persons with truly pitiable circumstances will uniformly not be submitted—losing the intent of reverent compassion."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor said: "Yet I fear the circuits will become careless, and persons with truly pitiable circumstances will uniformly go unreported—contrary to reverent compassion.

sentences.zh: 令刑部坐條行下。

translations.literal: He ordered the Ministry of Justice to establish articles and promulgate them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Ministry of Justice to draft articles and promulgate them.

sentences.zh: 馴至乾道，讞獄之弊，日益滋甚。

translations.literal: Gradually reaching the Qiandao era, the abuses of case judgment daily grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qiandao era, abuses in the adjudication of cases had grown steadily worse.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乃詔有司緣情引條定斷，更不奏裁。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong then issued an edict that the offices, according to circumstances, cite articles to fix judgment, and no longer submit for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong then ordered that offices decide cases by citing statutes according to circumstance, without further submission for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 其後刑部侍郎方滋言：「有司斷罪，其間有情重法輕，情輕法重，情理可憫，刑名疑慮，命官犯罪，議親議故之類，難以一切定斷。

translations.literal: Later, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice Fang Zi stated: "When the offices judge guilt, among them are cases where circumstances are heavy and the law light, circumstances light and the law heavy, circumstances pitiable, charges doubtful, crimes by appointed officials, deliberation on kinship or prior acquaintance, and the like—difficult to fix judgment uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Vice Minister Fang Zi of the Ministry of Justice argued: "When offices pass judgment, some cases involve heavy circumstance and light law, light circumstance and heavy law, pitiable circumstances, doubtful charges, crimes by officials, deliberation on kinship or prior acquaintance, and the like—cases that cannot be decided uniformly.

sentences.zh: 今後宜於敕律條令，明言合奏裁事件，乞並依建隆三年敕文。」

translations.literal: Hereafter it is appropriate, in edicts, codes, and statutes, clearly to state events requiring submission for imperial decision; we beg to follow entirely the edict text of the third year of Jianlong."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter the edicts, code, and statutes should clearly list cases requiring imperial decision; we ask that the edict of the third year of Jianlong govern entirely.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，臣僚請：「今後大辟，只以為首應坐死罪者奏，為從不應坐死者，先次決遣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, officials requested: "Hereafter for capital punishment, only the ringleader who should sit the death penalty shall be submitted; accomplices who should not sit death shall first be decided and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, officials requested: "Henceforth in capital cases, only ringleaders liable to death shall be submitted; accomplices not liable to death shall be sentenced and dispatched first.

sentences.zh: 及流、徒罪，不許作情重取旨。

translations.literal: As for exile and hard-labor offenses, seeking imperial direction on grounds of heavy circumstances shall not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For exile and hard-labor offenses, seeking imperial direction on grounds of heavy circumstance shall not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 不然，則坐以不應奏而奏之罪。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, charge with the offense of submitting though submission was not appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise charge the offense of improper submission.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 至理宗時，往往讞不時報，囚多瘐死。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Lizong, often cases for judgment were not reported in time, and many prisoners died of illness in detention.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Lizong's reign, case reports were often delayed, and many prisoners died of illness awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 監察御史程元鳳奏曰：「今罪無輕重，悉皆送獄，獄無大小，悉皆稽留。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Cheng Yuanfeng submitted a memorial, saying: "Now without distinction of light or heavy guilt, all are sent to prison; without distinction of large or small prison, all are detained.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Cheng Yuanfeng memorialized: "Now guilt light or heavy alike is sent to prison; prison great or small alike holds prisoners in prolonged detention.

sentences.zh: 或以追索未齊而不問，或以供款未圓而不呈，或以書擬未當而不判，獄官視以為常，而不顧其遲，獄吏留以為利，而惟恐其速。

translations.literal: Some, because recovery was not complete, would not pursue the case; some, because confession was not complete, would not submit it; some, because the draft judgment was improper, would not decide it. Prison officials regarded this as normal and paid no heed to delay; prison clerks detained cases for profit and feared only that they be resolved too quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Cases stalled when restitution was incomplete, confessions unfinished, or draft judgments flawed. Prison officials treated delay as routine; clerks profited from detention and dreaded swift resolution.

sentences.zh: 奏案申牘既下刑部，遲延日月方送理寺。

translations.literal: Once memorial cases and submission documents had reached the Ministry of Justice, months would pass before they were sent to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial cases sent to the Ministry of Justice often languished for months before reaching the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 理寺看詳，亦復如之。

translations.literal: The Court's review was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Court's review proceeded no faster.

sentences.zh: 寺回申部，部回申省，動涉歲月。

translations.literal: The Court reported back to the Ministry, the Ministry reported back to the Secretariat—often involving months.
translations.idiomatic: The Court reported to the Ministry, the Ministry to the Secretariat—each leg consuming months.

sentences.zh: 省房又未遽為呈擬，亦有呈擬而疏駮者，疏駮歲月，又復如前。

translations.literal: The Secretariat offices also did not promptly prepare draft submissions; some draft submissions met with memorial rebuttal; after months of rebuttal, it was again as before.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat offices delayed draft submissions; when rebuttals came, months passed in reply—and the cycle began anew.

sentences.zh: 展轉遲回，有一二年未報下者。

translations.literal: Turning and turning in delay, some went one or two years without a report being issued.
translations.idiomatic: Passed from office to office, some cases went one or two years without a final report.

sentences.zh: 可疑可矜，法當奏讞，矜而全之，乃反遲回。

translations.literal: Cases that were doubtful and pitiable, by law requiring submission for judgment—pity could spare them—yet instead were delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Cases doubtful yet pitiable, which by law merited submission for judgment and might have been spared, were instead left to languish.

sentences.zh: 有矜貸之報下，而其人已斃於獄者；

translations.literal: Some had reports of commutation for pity issued down, yet the person had already died in prison;
translations.idiomatic: Some received commutation reports only after they had already died in prison;

sentences.zh: 有犯者獲貸，而干連病死不一者，豈不重可念哉？

translations.literal: Some offenders received commutation while those implicated by connection died of illness—not a few; was this not deeply lamentable?
translations.idiomatic: Some offenders were spared while persons implicated in their cases died in custody—not a few. Was this not deeply lamentable?

sentences.zh: 請自今諸路奏讞，即以所發月日申御史臺，從臺臣究省、部、法寺之慢。」

translations.literal: We request that from now on, for all circuit submissions for judgment, the month and day of dispatch be reported to the Censorate, so that censorial officials may investigate the slowness of the Secretariat, Ministry, and Court of Judicial Review."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter every circuit submission for judgment report its dispatch date to the Censorate, so censors may investigate delays by the Secretariat, Ministry of Justice, and Court of Judicial Review."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 而所司延滯，尋復如舊。

translations.literal: But the responsible offices delayed, and soon it was again as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible offices continued to stall, and before long matters were as bad as ever.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，乃下詔曰：「比詔諸提刑司，取翻異駁勘之獄，從輕斷決。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding, an edict was issued, saying: "Recently we issued an edict the judicial intendant offices to take cases of reversed verdict and re-examination and decide leniently.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingding, an edict declared: "We recently ordered judicial intendant offices to take cases involving reversed verdicts and re-examination and decide them leniently.

sentences.zh: 而長吏監司多不任責，又引奏裁，甚者有十餘年不決之獄。

translations.literal: Yet prefects and supervisory commissioners often did not accept responsibility, again citing submission for imperial decision; in extreme cases there were cases unresolved for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prefects and supervisory commissioners often shirked responsibility, again resorting to submission for imperial decision; some cases went unresolved for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 仰提刑司守臣審勘，或前勘未盡，委有可疑，除命官、命婦、宗婦、宗女及合用蔭人奏裁外，其餘斷訖以聞。

translations.literal: We expect judicial intendant offices and local officials to examine cases; where prior examination was incomplete and there is truly doubt—except for appointed officials, wives of officials, imperial clan wives, imperial clan daughters, and persons eligible for yin privilege, who require submission for imperial decision—all others shall decide and report.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial intendant offices and local officials must examine cases thoroughly. Where prior review was incomplete and doubt remains—except for appointed officials, officials' wives, imperial clan women, and persons eligible for yin privilege, who still require imperial decision—all others shall decide and report.

sentences.zh: 官吏特免收坐一次。」

translations.literal: Officials and clerks shall once be specially exempted from seated punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Officials and clerks shall receive one special exemption from accountability."

sentences.zh: 凡應配役者傅軍籍，用重典者黥其面。

translations.literal: All who should be assigned to penal service were entered in military registers; those subjected to severe punishment had their faces tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Those sentenced to penal service were enrolled in military registers; those subject to severe punishment were tattooed on the face.

sentences.zh: 會赦，則有司上其罪狀，情輕者，縱之；

translations.literal: When an amnesty occurred, the offices submitted their offense records; those whose circumstances were light were released;
translations.idiomatic: At amnesty, offices submitted offense records; those whose circumstances were light were released;

sentences.zh: 重者，終身不釋。

translations.literal: those heavy, were never released for life.
translations.idiomatic: those whose circumstances were grave remained confined for life.

sentences.zh: 初，徒罪非有官當贖銅者，在京師則隸將作監役，兼役之宮中，或輸作左校、右校役。

translations.literal: Initially, for hard-labor offenses without official rank to offset or redemption by copper, in the capital they were assigned to the Directorate of Palace Works, also serving in the palace, or submitted labor to the Left and Right Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: At first, hard-labor offenders in the capital who lacked official rank to offset punishment or copper to redeem it were assigned to the Directorate of Palace Works—some serving in the palace, others laboring at the Left and Right Workshops.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，御史臺言：「若此者，雖有其名，無復役使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, the Censorate stated: "For such persons, though they had the name, there was no actual service.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao, the Censorate reported: "Such persons existed in name only and performed no actual labor.

sentences.zh: 遇祠祭，供水火，則有本司供官。

translations.literal: When sacrifices occurred and water and fire were supplied, there were supply officials of the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices, when water and fire were needed, the responsible office provided its own officials.

sentences.zh: 望令大理依格斷遣。」

translations.literal: We hope the Court of Judicial Review will decide and dispatch according to regulations."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Court of Judicial Review decide and dispatch them according to statute.

sentences.zh: 於是並送作坊役之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were sent to serve in the workshops.
translations.idiomatic: All were then sent to serve in the workshops.

sentences.zh: 太宗以國初諸方割據，沿五代之制，罪人率配隸西北邊，多亡投塞外，誘羌為寇，乃詔：「當徒者，勿復隸秦州、靈武、通遠軍及緣邊諸郡。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, because at the founding of the realm the regions were divided and held by separate powers, following the system of the Five Dynasties, criminals were generally assigned to the northwestern border; many fled beyond the frontier and incited the Qiang to raid. He therefore issued an edict: "Those liable to hard labor shall no longer be assigned to Qinzhou, Lingwu, Tongyuan Army, and the frontier prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the realm, when regions remained divided, Emperor Taizong followed the Five Dynasties practice of assigning criminals to the northwestern frontier. Many fled beyond the border and incited Qiang raids. He therefore decreed: "Hard-labor offenders shall no longer be assigned to Qinzhou, Lingwu, Tongyuan Army, or other frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時江、廣已平，乃皆流南方。

translations.literal: At that time Jiang and Guang had been pacified, so all were exiled to the south.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangnan and Lingnan now pacified, all were exiled southward.

sentences.zh: 先是，犯死罪獲貸者，多配隸登州沙門島及通州海島，皆有屯兵使者領護。

translations.literal: Previously, those who committed death offenses and received commutation were mostly assigned to Dengzhou's Shamen Island and Tongzhou's sea islands; both had garrison troops and envoys overseeing them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, death-sentence offenders who received commutation were mostly sent to Shamen Island off Dengzhou and the sea islands of Tongzhou, each guarded by garrison troops under supervising envoys.

sentences.zh: 而通州島中凡兩處官鹽，豪強難制者隸崇明鎮，懦弱者隸東州市。

translations.literal: On Tongzhou's islands there were in all two government saltworks; the powerful and hard to control were assigned to Chongming garrison; the weak were assigned to Dongsuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou's islands held two government saltworks. The strong and unruly were assigned to Chongming garrison; the weak, to Dongsuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，始令分隸鹽亭役之，而沙門如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, it was first ordered that they be divided and assigned to salt pavilions for service, while Shamen remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, offenders were first divided among salt pavilions for labor, while Shamen Island assignments continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，詔免嶺南流配荷校執役。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, an edict exempted exiles assigned to Lingnan from carrying cangues and performing corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong, an edict freed Lingnan exiles from wearing cangues and performing corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 初，婦人有罪至流，亦執鍼配役。

translations.literal: Initially, when women were guilty to the point of exile, they also carried needles and were assigned to penal service.
translations.idiomatic: At first, women sentenced to exile also carried needles and were assigned to penal service.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔罷免之。

translations.literal: At this point, an edict abolished this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict now abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 始令雜犯至死貸命者，勿流沙門島，止隸諸州牢城。

translations.literal: It was first ordered that those guilty of miscellaneous offenses reaching death who received commuted sentences should not be sent to Shamen Island, but only assigned to various prefectures' prison fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: It was first ordered that offenders guilty of miscellaneous capital crimes who received commuted sentences should not be sent to Shamen Island but assigned only to prefectural prison fortresses.

sentences.zh: 舊制，僮僕有犯，得私黥其面。

translations.literal: Under the old system, when servants committed offenses, masters could privately tattoo their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, masters could privately tattoo the faces of offending servants.

sentences.zh: 帝謂：「僮使受傭，本良民也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Servants hired for employment are originally good commoners."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Hired servants are ordinary law-abiding people.

sentences.zh: 詔：「盜主財者，杖脊、黥面配牢城，勿私黥之。

translations.literal: An edict: "Those who steal their master's property—caning, facial tattoo, assignment to prison fortress; do not privately tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Servants who steal their master's property shall be caned, tattooed, and assigned to a prison fortress—not privately marked by their masters.

sentences.zh: 十貫以上，配五百里外；

translations.literal: Ten strings of cash or more—assign five hundred li away;
translations.idiomatic: Thefts of ten strings of cash or more: assign five hundred li away;

sentences.zh: 二十貫以上，奏裁。」

translations.literal: twenty strings or more—submit for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: twenty strings or more: submit for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 帝欲寬配隸之刑 ，祥符六年，詔審刑院、大理寺、三司詳定以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to lighten the punishment of penal assignment; in the sixth year of Xiangfu, he issued an edict the Office of Review of Penalties, Court of Judicial Review, and Three Commissions to review in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to lighten penal assignment, the emperor in the sixth year of Xiangfu ordered the Office of Review of Penalties, the Court of Judicial Review, and the Three Commissions to review the statutes in detail and report.

sentences.zh: 既而取犯茶鹽礬麴、私鑄造軍器、市外蕃香藥、挾銅錢誘漢口出界、主吏盜貨官物、夜聚為妖，比舊法咸從輕減。

translations.literal: Soon after, for offenses of tea, salt, alum, and yeast monopolies; private forging of weapons; buying foreign aromatics and medicines outside permitted channels; carrying copper cash to induce Han people to cross the border; chief clerks stealing government goods; gathering at night for sorcery—all compared to the old law were leniently reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, penalties were leniently reduced below the old standard for monopoly violations involving tea, salt, alum, and yeast; private weapon forging; illicit purchase of foreign aromatics and medicines; inducing Han subjects to cross the border with copper cash; chief clerks stealing government goods; and nocturnal gatherings for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 乾興以前，州軍長吏，往往擅配罪人。

translations.literal: Before Qianxing, prefectural and military commanders often on their own authority assigned criminals.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Qianxing era, prefects and military commanders often assigned criminals on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，首下詔禁止，且令情非巨者，須奏待報。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he first issued an edict forbidding this, and ordered that where circumstances were not grave, submission and awaiting response was required.
translations.idiomatic: Upon acceding, Emperor Renzong first forbade unauthorized assignment and required submission and imperial approval except where circumstances were grave.

sentences.zh: 又詔諸路按察官，取乾興赦前配隸兵籍者，列所坐罪狀以聞。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered circuit inspection officials to take those assigned to military registers before the Qianxing amnesty, list their offenses, and report.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered circuit inspectors to review those enrolled in military registers before the Qianxing amnesty, list their offenses, and report.

sentences.zh: 自是赦書下，輒及之。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever amnesty edicts were issued, this was included.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every amnesty edict included this provision.

sentences.zh: 初，京師裁造院募女工，而軍士妻有罪，皆配隸南北作坊。

translations.literal: Initially, the capital's garment manufacturing bureau recruited women workers, and soldiers' wives who committed offenses were all assigned to the northern and southern workshops.
translations.idiomatic: At first the capital's garment bureau recruited women workers, and soldiers' wives convicted of offenses were all assigned to the northern and southern workshops.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，特詔釋之，聽自便。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, a special edict released them and allowed them to go as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tiansheng era, a special edict released them and allowed them to go free.

sentences.zh: 婦人應配，則以妻務或軍營致遠務卒之無家者，著為法。

translations.literal: Women who should be assigned—then wives of corvée workers or homeless far-service soldiers in military camps—were established as law.
translations.idiomatic: For women subject to assignment, the law now specified wives of corvée workers or homeless far-service soldiers in military camps.

sentences.zh: 時又詔曰：「聞配徒者，其妻子流離道路，罕能生還，朕甚憐之。

translations.literal: At the time another edict said: "We hear that for those assigned to hard labor, their wives and children wander the roads and rarely survive to return—we deeply pity them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "We hear that the wives and children of hard-labor assignees wander the roads and rarely survive the journey—we are deeply moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 自今應配者，錄具獄刑名及所配地里，上尚書刑部詳覆。」

translations.literal: From now on for those who should be assigned, record the full case, punishment name, and place of assignment; submit to the Ministry of Justice for detailed review."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, before any assignment, record the full case, the sentence, and the destination, and submit to the Ministry of Justice for review.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又詔應配者，須長吏以下集聽事慮問。

translations.literal: Before long, another edict: those to be assigned must have the chief official and below assemble in the hall of audience for deliberative inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, another edict required the chief official and subordinates to assemble in the hall of audience and deliberate before any assignment.

sentences.zh: 後以奏牘煩冗，罷錄具獄，第以單狀上承進司。

translations.literal: Later because memorial documents were burdensome, recording full cases was abolished; only single summaries were submitted to the Forwarding Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because memorial paperwork grew burdensome, full-case records were dropped; only summary sheets were sent to the Forwarding Office.

sentences.zh: 既又罷慮問焉。

translations.literal: Soon after, deliberative inquiry was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberative inquiry was abolished soon after.

sentences.zh: 知益州薛田言：「蜀人配徒他路者，請雖老疾毋得釋。」

translations.literal: Prefect of Yizhou Xue Tian stated: "For Shu people assigned as hard laborers to other circuits, we request that even if old or ill they not be released."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tian, prefect of Yizhou, petitioned: "Shu natives assigned to hard labor in other circuits should not be released even when old or infirm.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遠民無知犯法，終身不得還鄉里，豈朕意哉？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Distant commoners, ignorant, break the law, and never return home—is this our intent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Ignorant people from distant regions break the law and never see home again—is that my intent?

sentences.zh: 察其情可矜者許還。」

translations.literal: Examine those whose circumstances are pitiable and permit return."
translations.idiomatic: Examine those whose circumstances warrant pity and permit them to return.

sentences.zh: 後復詔罪狀獷惡者勿許。

translations.literal: Later another edict: those whose offenses were brutal and vicious were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: A later edict barred return for those whose offenses were brutal and vicious.

sentences.zh: 初，令配隸罪人皆奏待報，既而繫獄淹久，奏請煩數。

translations.literal: Initially it was ordered that all criminals assigned to penal service submit and await response; soon cases piled up in prison for long periods and submissions became frequent.
translations.idiomatic: At first all penal assignments required submission and imperial approval; but prolonged detention and frequent petitions soon followed.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，乃詔有司參酌輕重，著為令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, it was issued an edict that the offices weigh light and heavy and establish it as ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao, offices were ordered to weigh cases by severity and codify the rules.

sentences.zh: 凡命官犯重罪，當配隸，則於外州編管，或隸牙校。

translations.literal: All appointed officials who committed serious crimes and should be assigned were placed under registered supervision in outer prefectures, or assigned to military adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed officials guilty of serious crimes subject to assignment were placed under registered supervision in outer prefectures or assigned to military adjutants.

sentences.zh: 其坐死特貸者，多杖、黥配遠州牢城，經恩量移，始免軍籍。

translations.literal: Those who sat death but received special commutation—mostly caning, tattoo, assignment to distant prefecture prison fortresses; only after amnesty and measured transfer were they released from military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Those liable to death but specially commuted were mostly caned, tattooed, and sent to distant prison fortresses; only after amnesty and measured transfer were they removed from military registers.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，吏同時以贓敗者數人，悉竄之嶺南，下詔申儆在位。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, several officials simultaneously failed for bribery; all were banished to Lingnan; an edict was issued to warn those in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiansheng era, several officials fell together on bribery charges and were all banished to Lingnan; an edict warned those still in office.

sentences.zh: 有平羌縣尉鄭宗諤者，受賕枉法抵死，會赦當奪官。

translations.literal: There was Pingqiang County Captain Zheng Zonge, who took bribes and perverted the law, liable to death; amnesty came and he should have been stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Pingqiang County Captain Zheng Zonge took bribes and perverted the law, warranting death; an amnesty arrived and he should have been stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 帝問輔臣曰：「尉奉月幾何，豈祿薄不足自養邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked his chief ministers: "What is a captain's monthly salary—can it be that the stipend is too thin to support oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his chief ministers: "What does a county captain earn each month? Can his stipend truly be too small to live on?

sentences.zh: 王欽若對曰：「奉雖薄，廉士固亦自守。」

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo replied: "Though the salary is thin, men of integrity still maintain themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo answered: "The salary is modest, but men of integrity manage nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 特杖宗諤，配隸安州。

translations.literal: Zonge was specially caned and assigned to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge was specially caned and assigned to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後數懲貪吏，至其末年，吏知以廉自飾，犯法者稍損於舊矣。

translations.literal: After this corruption was punished several times; by the end of his reign officials knew to adorn themselves with integrity, and lawbreakers were somewhat reduced from before.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials were punished repeatedly thereafter; by the end of his reign officials had learned to cultivate an appearance of integrity, and offenses declined somewhat.

sentences.zh: 罪人貸死者，舊多配沙門島，至者多死。

translations.literal: Commuted death-sentence criminals were formerly mostly assigned to Shamen Island; most who arrived died.
translations.idiomatic: Commuted capital offenders were once mostly sent to Shamen Island, where most died.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，詔當配沙門島者，第配廣南地牢城 ；

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era, edict: those who should be assigned to Shamen Island were only assigned to Guangnan prison fortresses;
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyou era, an edict directed Shamen-bound offenders to Guangnan prison fortresses instead;

sentences.zh: 廣南罪人，乃配嶺北。

translations.literal: Guangnan criminals were then assigned north of the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnan offenders were in turn assigned north of the Ling range.

sentences.zh: 然其後又有配沙門島者。

translations.literal: Yet afterward some were again assigned to Shamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward some were again sent to Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，既疏理天下繫囚，因詔諸路配役人皆釋之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, having reviewed all prisoners in the realm, an edict was issued to release all penal laborers in the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingli, after a review of prisoners empire-wide, an edict released all penal laborers in the circuits.

sentences.zh: 六年，又詔曰：「如聞百姓抵輕罪，而長吏擅刺隸他州，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, another edict: "We hear that commoners guilty of light offenses are on their own authority branded and assigned to other prefectures by chief officials—we deeply pity this.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, another edict declared: "We hear that chief officials are branding commoners guilty of minor offenses and assigning them to other prefectures on their own authority—we are deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 自今非得於法外從事者，毋得輒刺罪人。」

translations.literal: From now on except where permitted to act outside the law, do not rashly brand criminals."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, except where the law expressly permits otherwise, officials shall not rashly brand offenders.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，既赦，命知制誥曾公亮、李絢閱所配人罪狀以聞，於是多所寬縱。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, after amnesty, edict writers Zeng Gongliang and Li Xuan were ordered to review the offense records of assigned persons and report; many were leniently released.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, after an amnesty, edict drafters Zeng Gongliang and Li Xuan were ordered to review assignees' records and report; many were leniently released.

sentences.zh: 公亮請著為故事，且請益、梓、利、夔四路就委轉運、鈐轄司閱之。

translations.literal: Gongliang requested this be established as precedent, and requested that in the four circuits of Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui review be delegated to transport and military supervision offices.
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang asked that this become standing practice and that in the Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui circuits review be delegated to transport and military supervision offices.

sentences.zh: 自後每赦命官，率以為常。

translations.literal: From then on at every amnesty, officials appointed to this became routine.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter such review appointments became routine at every amnesty.

sentences.zh: 配隸重者沙門島砦，其次嶺表，其次三千里至鄰州，其次羈管，其次遷鄉。

translations.literal: Penal assignment: most severe—Shamen Island fortress; next—south of the Ling; next—three thousand li to neighboring prefecture; next—restricted supervision; next—return to home district.
translations.idiomatic: Penal assignment ranked from most to least severe: Shamen Island fortress; then the Lingnan region; then exile up to three thousand li to a neighboring prefecture; then restricted supervision; then relocation within one's home district.

sentences.zh: 斷訖，不以寒暑，即時上道。

translations.literal: Once judgment was complete, regardless of cold or heat, they immediately set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Once sentence was passed, offenders set out immediately, regardless of season.

sentences.zh: 吳充建請：「流人冬寒被創，上道多凍死。

translations.literal: Wu Chong memorialized: "Exiles in winter cold with wounds—many freeze to death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong memorialized: "Exiles travel in winter wounded and cold; many freeze to death on the road.

sentences.zh: 請自今非情理巨，遇冬月聽留役本處，至春月遣之。」

translations.literal: We request from now on, unless circumstances are grave, in winter months permit them to remain serving locally until spring when they are dispatched."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter, except in grave cases, winter departures be deferred: let offenders remain and serve locally until spring.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，比部郎中、知房州張仲宣嘗檄巡檢體究金州金阬，無甚利。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Bureau of Review Director and Prefect of Fangzhou Zhang Zhongxuan once dispatched an inspector to investigate Jinzhou's gold mine—there was little profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xining, Zhang Zhongxuan, director of the Bureau of Review and prefect of Fangzhou, once dispatched an inspector to investigate a Jinzhou gold mine and found little profit in it.

sentences.zh: 土人憚興作，以金八兩求仲宣不差官。

translations.literal: Local people feared the construction work and offered Zhongxuan eight taels of gold so he would not dispatch officials.
translations.idiomatic: Locals, fearing the project, offered Zhongxuan eight taels of gold to keep officials from being dispatched.

sentences.zh: 及事覺，法官坐仲宣枉法贓應絞，援前比貸死，杖脊、黥配海島。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, the judicial officer found Zhongxuan liable for perverting the law and taking bribes, warranting strangulation; citing prior precedent he was commuted from death, caned, tattooed, and assigned to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter came to light, the judge found Zhongxuan guilty of perverting the law and taking bribes, warranting strangulation; citing precedent, he was commuted from death, caned, tattooed, and assigned to a sea island.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院蘇頌言：「仲宣所犯，可比恐喝條。

translations.literal: Director of the Office of Review of Penalties Su Song stated: "Zhongxuan's offense can be compared to the article on intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song, director of the Office of Review of Penalties, argued: "Zhongxuan's offense fits the statute on intimidation.

sentences.zh: 且古者『刑不上大夫』，仲宣官五品，有罪得乘車，今刑為徒隸，其人雖無足矜，恐污辱衣冠爾。」

translations.literal: Moreover in antiquity 'punishment does not reach great officers'; Zhongxuan is fifth rank, when guilty may ride in a cart; now punishment makes him a penal laborer—the person himself may not warrant pity, but we fear disgrace to the robes and caps."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, antiquity held that 'punishment does not reach great officers.' Zhongxuan is fifth rank and, when guilty, may still ride in a carriage; to reduce him to penal servitude may not pity the man himself, but it would disgrace the office he represents.

sentences.zh: 遂免杖、黥，流賀州。

translations.literal: Thereupon caning and tattoo were waived; he was exiled to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Caning and tattoo were waived; he was exiled to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 自是命官無杖、黥法。

translations.literal: From then on appointed officials had no law of caning and tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter appointed officials were no longer subject to caning and tattoo.

sentences.zh: 六年，審刑院言：「登州沙門砦配隸，以二百人為額，餘則移置海外，非禁姦之意。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Office of Review stated: "Dengzhou Shamen fortress penal assignment has a quota of two hundred persons; the remainder are moved overseas—not the intent of restraining wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Office of Review reported: "Shamen fortress at Dengzhou holds a quota of two hundred assignees; overflow is sent overseas—hardly the purpose of restraining wickedness.

sentences.zh: 詔以三百人為額。

translations.literal: The edict set the quota at three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The quota was raised to three hundred.

sentences.zh: 廣南轉運司言：「春州瘴癘之地，配隸至者十死八九，願停配罪人。」

translations.literal: Guangnan Transport Commission stated: "Chunzhou is a miasma-ridden place; of those assigned there eight or nine of ten die—we wish to stop assigning criminals there."
translations.idiomatic: The Guangnan Transport Commission reported: "Chunzhou is malarial; eight or nine of ten assignees die there. We ask that criminals no longer be sent there.

sentences.zh: 詔：「應配沙門島者，許配春州，餘勿配。」

translations.literal: Edict: "Those who should be assigned to Shamen Island may be assigned to Chunzhou; others do not assign there."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Offenders bound for Shamen Island may be sent to Chunzhou; no others shall be assigned there.

sentences.zh: 既而諸配隸除凶盜外，少壯者並寘河州，止五百人。

translations.literal: Soon after, of all penal assignees except violent robbers, young and strong were all placed in Hezhou, limited to five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, all able-bodied assignees except violent robbers were placed at Hezhou, capped at five hundred.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗以流人去鄉邑，疾死於道，而護送禁卒，往來勞費，用張誠一之議，隨所在配諸軍重役。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Shenzong, because exiles left home districts, died of illness on the road, and escort prison soldiers entailed back-and-forth labor and expense, adopted Zhang Chengyi's proposal—wherever they were, assign them to various armies for heavy corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Shenzong, seeing exiles leave home, die on the road, and burden escort guards with costly round trips, adopted Zhang Chengyi's proposal to assign them wherever they were to army heavy labor.

sentences.zh: 後中丞黃履等言，罷之。

translations.literal: Later Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Lü and others spoke, and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Lü and others objected, and the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 凡犯盜，刺環於耳後：徒、流，方；

translations.literal: All who commit theft—brand a ring behind the ear: for hard labor and exile, square;
translations.idiomatic: All thieves were branded with a ring behind the ear: square for hard labor and exile;

sentences.zh: 杖，圓；

translations.literal: for caning, round;
translations.idiomatic: round for caning;

sentences.zh: 三犯杖，移於面。

translations.literal: three caning offenses, move to the face.
translations.idiomatic: after three caning offenses, the mark was moved to the face.

sentences.zh: 徑不過五分。

translations.literal: Diameter not exceeding five fen.
translations.idiomatic: The mark's diameter was not to exceed five fen.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年， 刑部言：「諸配隸沙門島，強盜殺人縱火，贓滿五萬錢、強姦毆傷兩犯至死，累贓至二十萬錢、謀殺致死，及十惡死罪，造蠱已殺人者，不移配。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou, the Ministry of Justice stated: "For all assigned to Shamen Island—robbery, murder, arson; theft reaching fifty thousand cash; rape or assault causing death on a second offense; cumulative theft reaching two hundred thousand cash; murder by plotting; the ten abominations warranting death; and those who manufacture gu poison and have already killed—do not transfer assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanyou, the Ministry of Justice reported: "Those assigned to Shamen Island for robbery, murder, or arson; theft of fifty thousand cash; rape or assault causing death on a second offense; cumulative theft of two hundred thousand cash; plotted murder; the ten capital abominations; or manufacture of gu poison after a killing—shall not be transferred elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 強盜徒黨殺人不同謀，贓滿二十五萬，遇赦移配廣南，溢額者配隸遠惡。

translations.literal: Robbers in a gang who killed without common conspiracy, when stolen goods reached two hundred fifty thousand cash, upon amnesty were transferred in assignment to Guangnan; those exceeding quota were registered for penal servitude in remote and harsh places.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits who killed without having conspired together, when booty reached two hundred fifty thousand cash, were reassigned to Guangnan upon amnesty; those beyond the quota were sent to penal servitude in the remotest regions.

sentences.zh: 餘犯遇赦移配荊湖南北、福建路諸州，溢額者配隸廣南。

translations.literal: Remaining offenders, upon amnesty, were transferred in assignment to prefectures in Jinghu South and North and Fujian circuits; those exceeding quota were registered for penal servitude in Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: All other offenders, upon amnesty, were reassigned to prefectures in the Jinghu South and North and Fujian circuits; those beyond the quota were sent to penal servitude in Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 在沙門島滿五年，遇赦不該移配與不許縱還而年及六十以上者，移配廣南。

translations.literal: Those who had completed five years on Shamen Island, who upon amnesty were not eligible for transferred assignment or for release and return but were sixty years of age or older, were transferred in assignment to Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners who had served five years on Shamen Island and, though ineligible for reassignment or release under an amnesty, were sixty or older, were reassigned to Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 在島十年者，依餘犯格移配。

translations.literal: Those who had been on the island ten years were transferred in assignment according to the regulations for remaining offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had spent ten years on the island were reassigned under the rules governing other offenders.

sentences.zh: 篤疾或年及七十在島三年以上，移配近鄉州軍。

translations.literal: Those with grave illness, or who were seventy years of age or older and had been on the island three years or more, were transferred in assignment to prefectures and commands near their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: The gravely ill, and those seventy or older who had been on the island at least three years, were reassigned to prefectures and garrisons near their native places.

sentences.zh: 犯狀應移而老疾者同。

translations.literal: Those whose offenses warranted transfer but who were aged or ill were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders whose crimes called for reassignment but who were aged or infirm received the same treatment.

sentences.zh: 其永不放還者，各加二年移配。」

translations.literal: Those never to be released and returned, in each case had two years added before transferred assignment."
translations.idiomatic: For those never eligible for release, two years were added before reassignment.

sentences.zh: 後又定令：「沙門島已溢額，移配瓊州、萬安軍、昌化、朱崖軍。」

translations.literal: Later another regulation was fixed: "When Shamen Island had exceeded its quota, transfer assignment to Qiongzhou, Wan'an Army, Changhua, and Zhuya Army."
translations.idiomatic: Later a further statute was enacted: when Shamen Island exceeded its quota, prisoners were to be reassigned to Qiongzhou, Wan'an Army, Changhua, and Zhuya Army.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，刑部侍郎邢恕等言：「藝祖初定天下，主典自盜，贓滿者往往抵死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice Xing Shu and others stated: "When Emperor Taizu first settled the realm, chief clerks who embezzled on their own authority, when stolen goods reached the statutory threshold, were often punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 3 (1096), Vice Minister Xing Shu of the Ministry of Justice and others memorialized: "When Emperor Taizu first pacified the empire, chief clerks guilty of embezzlement on their own authority, once booty reached the statutory threshold, were often executed.

sentences.zh: 仁祖之初，尚不廢也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Renzong's reign, this was still not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Renzong's reign, the practice had not yet been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其後用法稍寬，官吏犯自盜，罪至極法，率多貸死。

translations.literal: Afterward the application of law grew somewhat lenient; when officials and clerks committed embezzlement on their own authority and the offense reached the maximum penalty, in most cases death was commuted.
translations.idiomatic: Later the law was applied more leniently: when officials and clerks embezzled on their own authority and the offense warranted the maximum penalty, death was usually commuted.

sentences.zh: 然甚者猶決刺配島，錢仙芝帶館職，李希甫歷轉運使，不免也。

translations.literal: Yet in the most serious cases they were still sentenced to tattooing and assigned to the island; Qian Xianzhi, though holding a court appointment, and Li Xifu, though having served as transport commissioner, were not spared.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the gravest cases still ended in tattooing and assignment to the island—Qian Xianzhi, who held a court appointment, and Li Xifu, a former transport commissioner, were not spared.

sentences.zh: 比朝廷用法益寬，主典人吏軍司有犯，例各貸死，略無差別。

translations.literal: Recently the court's application of law has grown ever more lenient; when chief clerks, petty officials, and military clerks commit offenses, in every case death is commuted, with scarcely any distinction.
translations.idiomatic: More recently the court's law has grown still more lenient: when chief clerks, petty officials, and military clerks offend, death is commuted in every case, with almost no distinction among them.

sentences.zh: 欲望講述祖宗故事，凡自盜，計贓多者，間出睿斷，以肅中外。」

translations.literal: We desire to recount the precedents of the founding emperors: for all cases of embezzlement on one's own authority, where stolen goods are substantial, let the sovereign's sage decision be invoked from time to time, to bring discipline within and without."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the precedents of the founding emperors be invoked: in all cases of embezzlement on one's own authority involving substantial booty, let the throne's sage judgment be sought from time to time, to restore discipline at court and throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔：「今後應枉法自盜，罪至死、贓數多者，並取旨。」

translations.literal: An edict: "Hereafter, for all who corruptly embezzle on their own authority, where the offense reaches death and stolen goods are substantial, all shall seek imperial direction."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Henceforth, in all cases of corrupt embezzlement on one's own authority where the offense warrants death and the booty is substantial, imperial direction shall be sought."

sentences.zh: 或患加役流法太重，官有監驅之勞，而道路有奔亡之慮。

translations.literal: Some worried that the law of exile with added labor was too severe, that officials had the burden of supervision and escort, and that on the roads there was a danger of flight.
translations.idiomatic: Some worried that the law of exile with added labor was too severe, that officials had the burden of supervision and escort, and that on the roads there was a danger of flight.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌元豐中嘗建議：「請依古置圜土，取當流者治罪訖，首鉗足，晝則居作，夜則置之圜土。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, Su Song once proposed, “I request that, following antiquity, enclosed grounds be established. Those liable to exile, after punishment for their crimes is completed, should have collars on their necks and fetters on their feet; by day they should live and work, and by night they should be placed in the enclosed grounds.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfeng, Su Song once proposed, “I request that, following antiquity, enclosed grounds be established. Those liable to exile, after punishment for their crimes is completed, should have collars on their necks and fetters on their feet; by day they should live and work, and by night they should be placed in the enclosed grounds.

sentences.zh: 滿三歲而後釋，未滿歲而遇赦者，不原。

translations.literal: Only after a full three years should they be released; those who encounter amnesty before the years are complete should not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a full three years should they be released; those who encounter amnesty before the years are complete should not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 既釋，仍送本鄉，譏察出入。

translations.literal: After release, they should still be sent back to their native villages, with their comings and goings watched.
translations.idiomatic: After release, they should still be sent back to their native villages, with their comings and goings watched.

sentences.zh: 又三歲不犯，乃聽自如。」

translations.literal: Only after another three years without offense should they be allowed to act freely.”
translations.idiomatic: Only after another three years without offense should they be allowed to act freely.”

sentences.zh: 時未果行。

translations.literal: At the time this was not ultimately put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was not ultimately put into effect.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，始從蔡京之請，令諸州築圜土以居強盜貸死者。

translations.literal: During Chongning, Cai Jing’s request was first followed, ordering the prefectures to build enclosed grounds to house robbers whose death sentences had been commuted.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning, Cai Jing’s request was first followed, ordering the prefectures to build enclosed grounds to house robbers whose death sentences had been commuted.

sentences.zh: 晝則役作，夜則拘之，視罪之輕重，以為久近之限。

translations.literal: By day they performed labor, and by night they were confined; the length of term was set according to the severity of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: By day they performed labor, and by night they were confined; the length of term was set according to the severity of the crime.

sentences.zh: 許出圜土日充軍，無過者縱釋。

translations.literal: On the day they left the enclosed grounds, they were permitted to enter military service; those without faults were released.
translations.idiomatic: On the day they left the enclosed grounds, they were permitted to enter military service; those without faults were released.

sentences.zh: 行之二年，其法不便，乃罷。

translations.literal: After the system had been carried out for two years, the law proved inconvenient and was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the system had been carried out for two years, the law proved inconvenient and was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，復行。

translations.literal: In Daguan year 1, it was implemented again.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan year 1, it was implemented again.

sentences.zh: 四年，復罷。

translations.literal: In year 4, it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, it was again abolished.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，諸配隸，祥符編敕止四十六條，慶曆中，增至百七十餘條。

translations.literal: After the Southern crossing, for all registered penal servitude, the Xiangfu compiled edicts had only forty-six articles; in the Qingli era they increased to more than one hundred seventy articles.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south, registered penal servitude was governed by only forty-six articles in the Xiangfu compiled edicts; under Qingli this rose to more than one hundred seventy.

sentences.zh: 至於淳熙，又增至五百七十條，則四倍於慶曆矣。

translations.literal: By Chunxi it had again increased to five hundred seventy articles—four times the Qingli number.
translations.idiomatic: By the Chunxi era the total had reached five hundred seventy articles—four times the Qingli figure.

sentences.zh: 配法既多，犯者日眾，黥配之人，所至充斥。

translations.literal: Since assignment regulations had grown so numerous, offenders daily multiplied, and persons tattooed and assigned filled every place they reached.
translations.idiomatic: As assignment statutes multiplied, offenders grew ever more numerous, and tattooed convicts sent to penal servitude crowded every destination.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十一年，校書郎羅點言其太重，乃詔刑、寺集議奏聞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chunxi, Proofreader Luo Dian stated that the penalties were too severe; thereupon an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review to assemble for deliberation and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 11 (1184), Proofreader Luo Dian argued that penalties were too harsh; the throne ordered the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review to confer and report.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，未有定論。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year, no fixed conclusion had been reached.
translations.idiomatic: By Chunxi 14 (1187), no final decision had been reached.

sentences.zh: 其後臣僚議，以為：「若止居役，不離鄉井，則幾惠姦，不足以懲惡；

translations.literal: Later officials deliberated, holding that: "If one only imposes local labor service without leaving one's native place, one nearly favors wrongdoing and is insufficient to punish evil;
translations.idiomatic: Later officials deliberated, arguing: "If offenders are merely put to local labor without leaving their native places, wrongdoing is almost indulged and evil goes insufficiently punished;

sentences.zh: 若盡用配法，不恤黥刺，則面目一壞，誰復顧藉？

translations.literal: if one fully applies assignment regulations without regard for tattooing, then once the face is ruined, who will again show concern?
translations.idiomatic: if assignment statutes are applied in full without regard for tattooing, once a man's face is marred, who will care for him again?

sentences.zh: 強民適長威力，有過無由自新。

translations.literal: Violent men thereby grow in power, and when they err there is no path to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Violent men thereby grow bolder, and when they offend they have no way to reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 檢照元豐刑部格，諸編配人自有不移、不放及移放條限；

translations.literal: Examining the Yuanfeng Ministry of Justice regulations, persons under registered assignment had their own provisions on no transfer, no release, and limits on transfer and release;
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the Yuanfeng Ministry of Justice regulations, registered assignees had distinct rules governing non-transfer, non-release, and the limits on transfer and release;

sentences.zh: 政和編配格又有情重、稍重、情輕、稍輕四等。

translations.literal: the Zhenghe registered assignment regulations further had four grades: heavily culpable, somewhat heavy, lightly culpable, and somewhat light.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhenghe registered-assignment regulations further divided cases into four grades: heavily culpable, somewhat heavy, lightly culpable, and somewhat light.

sentences.zh: 若依倣舊格，稍加參訂，如入情重，則倣舊刺面，用不移不放之格；

translations.literal: If one follows the old regulations with slight revision, then for those entering the heavily culpable grade, tattoo the face as of old and apply the no-transfer, no-release regulations;
translations.idiomatic: If the old regulations are followed with modest revision, the heavily culpable would be face-tattooed as before and governed by the no-transfer, no-release rules;

sentences.zh: 其次稍重，則止刺額角，用配及十年之格；

translations.literal: next, the somewhat heavy would receive tattooing only on the forehead and temple, and the regulations for assignment with a ten-year term would apply;
translations.idiomatic: the somewhat heavy would be tattooed only on the forehead and temples and governed by the ten-year assignment rules;

sentences.zh: 其次稍輕，則與免黥刺，用不刺面、役滿放還之格；

translations.literal: next, the somewhat light would be exempted from tattooing and the regulations for no face tattoo, release upon completion of service would apply;
translations.idiomatic: the somewhat light would be exempt from tattooing and governed by the rules allowing release after service without facial marking;

sentences.zh: 其次最輕，則降為居役，別立年限縱免之格。

translations.literal: next, the lightest would be reduced to local labor service, with separate regulations setting a term for release and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: the lightest would be reduced to local labor service, with separate rules fixing a term for release and exemption.

sentences.zh: 儻有從坐編管，則置之本城，減其放限。

translations.literal: If any are accomplices subject to registered supervision, place them in the local prefectural city and reduce their term of release.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplices subject to registered supervision would remain in the prefectural seat, with their release term shortened.

sentences.zh: 如此，則於見行條法並無牴牾，且使刺面之法，專處情犯凶，而其他偶麗於罪，皆得全其面目，知所顧藉，可以自新。

translations.literal: Thus, existing statutes would not be contradicted, and the method of face tattooing would be reserved for offenses of heavy culpability and violence, while others who happened to fall under guilt could keep their faces intact, know that others would care for them, and be able to reform.
translations.idiomatic: In this way existing statutes would remain intact, face tattooing would be reserved for the heavily culpable and violent, and others who happened to fall afoul of the law could keep their faces unmarked, retain a sense of shame and standing, and find a path to reform.

sentences.zh: 省黥徒，銷姦黨，誠天下之切務。」

translations.literal: Reducing tattooed convicts and breaking up criminal cliques is truly an urgent task for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Reducing tattooed convicts and breaking criminal cliques is truly an urgent task for the empire.

sentences.zh: 即詔有司裁定，其後迄如舊制。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the offices to fix regulations; afterward matters continued as under the old system.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the offices to settle the matter; in the end the old system remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰四年，臣僚言：「配隸之人，蓋有兩等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiatai, officials stated: "Persons registered for penal servitude fall broadly into two grades.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiatai 4 (1204), officials memorialized: "Prisoners registered for penal servitude fall into two broad categories.

sentences.zh: 其鄉民一時鬥毆殺傷，及胥吏犯贓貸命流配等人，設使逃逸，未必能為大過，止欲從徒，配本州牢城重役，限滿給據，復為良民。

translations.literal: Country people who in a moment of brawling killed or wounded others, and clerks who embezzled and were spared death and sent into exile and assignment, even if they flee, may not necessarily commit great offenses; it is only desired that they be reduced from hard labor and assigned to heavy service in the local prefecture's penal fort, and upon completion of the term be given a certificate and restored as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers who kill or wound in sudden brawls, and clerks who embezzle and are spared death and exiled to penal servitude—even if they escape, they need not become great criminals; they should simply be demoted from hard labor to heavy service in the local penal fort, receive a certificate at term's end, and return to common life.

sentences.zh: 至於累犯強盜，及聚眾販賣私商，曾經殺傷捕獲之人，非村民、胥吏之比，欲並配屯駐軍，立為年限，限滿改刺從正軍。」

translations.literal: As for repeat robbers, those who gathered crowds to traffic in contraband, and those previously captured after killing or wounding— they are not comparable to villagers and clerks; it is desired that they all be assigned to garrison troops, a fixed term be established, and upon completion of the term they be tattooed again and enrolled in the regular army."
translations.idiomatic: Repeat robbers, smugglers who operate in gangs, and men previously captured after killing or wounding are another matter entirely; they should all be assigned to garrison troops for a fixed term, then tattooed again and enrolled in the regular army when the term expires.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 其所配之地，自高宗來，或配廣南海外四州，或配淮、漢、四川，迄度宗之世無定法，皆不足紀也。

translations.literal: As for the places of assignment, from Emperor Gaozong onward some were assigned to the four overseas prefectures of Guangnan, some to the Huai, Han, and Sichuan regions; down to the age of Emperor Duzong there was no fixed law, and none of this merits detailed record.
translations.idiomatic: As for where convicts were sent, from Emperor Gaozong onward some went to Guangnan's four overseas prefectures, others to the Huai, Han, and Sichuan regions; by Emperor Duzong's reign there was no fixed rule, and the details need not be recorded here.

sentences.zh: 凡內外所上刑獄，刑部、審刑院、大理寺參主之，又有糾察在京刑獄司以相審覆。

translations.literal: For all criminal cases submitted from within and without, the Ministry of Justice, the Court for Review of Penalties, and the Court of Judicial Review jointly presided; there was also the Inspectorate for Capital Penal Detentions to conduct mutual review.
translations.idiomatic: All criminal cases submitted from within and outside the capital were jointly handled by the Ministry of Justice, the Court for Review of Penalties, and the Court of Judicial Review; the Inspectorate for Capital Penal Detentions provided additional review.

sentences.zh: 官制既行，罷審刑 、糾察，歸其職於刑 部。

translations.literal: Once the new official system was implemented, the Court for Review of Penalties and the Inspectorate were abolished, and their duties returned to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the new official system took effect, the Court for Review of Penalties and the Inspectorate were abolished and their duties returned to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 四方之獄，則提點刑獄統治之。

translations.literal: Prisons in the four directions were under the unified governance of judicial intendants.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons throughout the realm were placed under judicial intendants.

sentences.zh: 官司之獄：在開封，有府司、左右軍巡院；

translations.literal: Prisons of government offices: in Kaifeng, there were the prefectural office and the Left and Right Military Patrol Courts;
translations.idiomatic: Government detention facilities in Kaifeng included the prefectural office and the Left and Right Military Patrol Courts;

sentences.zh: 在諸司，有殿前、馬步軍司及四排岸；

translations.literal: in the various bureaus, there were the Palace and Horse and Foot Army Commands and the Four River Patrols;
translations.idiomatic: within the central bureaus there were the Palace Command, the Horse and Foot Army Commands, and the Four River Patrols;

sentences.zh: 外則三京府司、左右軍巡院，諸州軍院、司理院，下至諸縣皆有獄。

translations.literal: outside, the Three Capital prefectural offices and Left and Right Military Patrol Courts, prefectural and command detention centers, judicial review courts, and down to every county—all had prisons.
translations.idiomatic: beyond the capital, the Three Capitals' prefectural offices and Military Patrol Courts, prefectural and garrison detention centers, judicial review courts, and even county jails all maintained prisons.

sentences.zh: 諸獄皆置樓牖，設漿鋪席，時具沐浴，食令溫暖，寒則給薪炭、衣物，暑則五日一滌枷杻。

translations.literal: All prisons were furnished with upper windows, bedding with padded mats, and regular bathing; food was to be kept warm, in cold weather fuel and clothing were supplied, and in summer the cangue and shackles were washed every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Every prison had ventilated upper windows, padded bedding, and regular bathing; food was served warm, fuel and clothing were provided in cold weather, and in summer cangues and shackles were cleaned every five days.

sentences.zh: 郡縣則所職之官躬行檢視，獄敝則修之使固。

translations.literal: In prefectures and counties the responsible officials personally inspected; when a prison was dilapidated they repaired it to make it secure.
translations.idiomatic: In prefectures and counties the responsible officials inspected in person; dilapidated prisons were repaired and secured.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位初，詔曰：「獄者，民命之所繫也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shenzong's accession, an edict stated: "Prisons are where the people's lives are bound.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shenzong's reign an edict declared: "Prisons hold the people's lives in the balance.

sentences.zh: 比聞有司歲考天下之奏，而多瘐死。

translations.literal: We have lately heard that when offices annually review memorials from the realm, many die of illness in detention.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately heard that in the annual review of reports from across the realm, many prisoners die of illness in detention.

sentences.zh: 深惟獄吏並緣為姦，檢視不明，使吾元元橫罹其害。

translations.literal: Deeply considering that prison clerks take advantage to commit wrongdoing and that inspections are unclear, causing our common people to suffer harm without cause.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection, prison clerks exploit their posts for corruption while inspections fail, causing innocent common people to suffer without cause.

sentences.zh: 書不云乎：『與其殺不辜，寧失不經。』

translations.literal: Does not the Classic say: 'Better to leave the unpunished than to execute the innocent'?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Classic say: 'Better to risk leaving the guilty unpunished than to execute the innocent'?

sentences.zh: 其具為令：應諸州軍巡司院所禁罪人，一歲在獄病死及二人，五縣以上州歲死三人，開封府司、軍巡歲死七人，推吏、獄卒皆杖六十，增一人則加一等，罪止杖一百。

translations.literal: Let regulations be drawn up: for all prisoners detained in patrol offices and courts of prefectures and commands, if two persons die of illness in prison within one year—or three in a prefecture of five counties or more, or seven in the Kaifeng prefectural office and Military Patrol Courts—the interrogators and jailers shall all receive sixty blows of the staff; for each additional death one degree is added, up to a maximum of one hundred blows.
translations.idiomatic: Draw up regulations: wherever two prisoners die of illness in detention within a year—or three in a prefecture of five counties or more, or seven in Kaifeng's prefectural office and Military Patrol Courts—all interrogators and jailers shall receive sixty blows of the staff; each additional death adds one degree of punishment, up to one hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 典獄官如推獄，經兩犯即坐從違制。

translations.literal: The prison warden, like the interrogator, upon a second offense is charged with violation of imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Prison wardens, like interrogators, face charges of violating imperial edict upon a second offense.

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄歲終會死者之數上之，中書檢察。

translations.literal: At year's end judicial intendants shall tally the number of deaths and submit them upward; the Secretariat shall inspect.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end judicial intendants shall tally deaths and report upward; the Secretariat shall review the figures.

sentences.zh: 死者過多，官吏雖已行罰，當更黜責。」

translations.literal: When deaths are excessive, even if officials have already been punished, they should further be dismissed and censured."
translations.idiomatic: When deaths are excessive, officials already punished should still face dismissal and further censure.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復詔：「失入死罪，已決三人，正官除名編管，貳者除名，次貳者免官勒停，吏配隸千里。

translations.literal: Before long, another edict: "For wrongful conviction of a capital offense, where three persons have already been executed—the principal official is stripped of name and placed under registered supervision, the second official is stripped of name, the third official is dismissed and compelled to retire, and clerks are registered for penal servitude a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward another edict followed: "For wrongful conviction in a capital case where three persons have already been executed—the principal official is stripped of rank and placed under registered supervision, the second official is stripped of rank, the third is dismissed and forced to retire, and clerks are sent to penal servitude a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 二人以下，視此有差。

translations.literal: For two persons or fewer, penalties differ accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: For two victims or fewer, penalties vary accordingly.

sentences.zh: 不以赦降、去官原免。

translations.literal: Amnesty, reduction of sentence, or departure from office shall not restore or exempt punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty, sentence reduction, or leaving office shall not restore rank or exempt punishment.

sentences.zh: 未決，則比類遞降一等；

translations.literal: If judgment has not yet been executed, then by analogy reduce one degree;
translations.idiomatic: If execution has not yet taken place, reduce the penalty by one degree by analogy;

sentences.zh: 赦降、去官，又減一等。

translations.literal: amnesty, reduction of sentence, or departure from office further reduces one degree.
translations.idiomatic: amnesty, sentence reduction, or leaving office reduces the penalty by one further degree.

sentences.zh: 令審刑院、刑部斷議官，歲終具嘗失入徒罪五人以上，京朝官展磨勘年，幕職、州縣官展考，或不與任滿指射差遣，或罷，仍即斷絕支賜。」

translations.literal: Order the adjudicating and deliberating officials of the Court for Review of Penalties and the Ministry of Justice that, at year's end, if they have wrongfully convicted five or more persons of penal servitude, metropolitan officials shall have their merit review years extended, staff and prefectural officials shall have their evaluations extended, or they shall be denied assignment at term's end, or dismissed—and their stipends shall immediately be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Adjudicating and deliberating officials of the Court for Review of Penalties and the Ministry of Justice who, by year's end, have wrongfully convicted five or more persons of penal servitude shall face extended merit review for metropolitan officials, extended evaluations for staff and prefectural officials, denial of assignment at term's end, or dismissal—with stipends immediately terminated.

sentences.zh: 以前法未備，故有是詔。

translations.literal: Because the earlier law was incomplete, there was this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Because earlier statutes were incomplete, this edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 又嘗詔：「官司失入人罪，而罪人應原免，官司猶論如法，即失出人罪；

translations.literal: There was also once an edict: "When a government office wrongfully convicts a person of an offense, yet the offender should be pardoned, and the office still judges according to law—that constitutes wrongful acquittal;
translations.idiomatic: An edict also stated: "When a government office wrongfully convicts someone who should in fact be pardoned, yet the office still applies the law as written, that counts as wrongful acquittal;

sentences.zh: 若應徒而杖，罪人應原免者，官司乃得用因罪人以致罪之律。」

translations.literal: if one should impose penal servitude but instead applies the bastinado, and the offender should be pardoned, the office may then apply the statute on incurring guilt through the offender."
translations.idiomatic: if penal servitude is warranted but flogging is imposed instead, and the offender should be pardoned, the office may then apply the statute on incurring guilt through the offender."

sentences.zh: 帝以國初廢大理獄非是，元豐元年詔曰：「大理有獄尚矣。

translations.literal: The emperor held that abolishing the Court of Judicial Review prison at the founding of the dynasty had been wrong. In the first year of Yuanfeng an edict stated: "The Court of Judicial Review has long maintained a prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that abolishing the Court of Judicial Review prison at the dynasty's founding had been a mistake. In the first year of Yuanfeng (1078) an edict declared: "The Court of Judicial Review has long maintained its own prison.

sentences.zh: 今中都官有所劾治，皆寓繫開封諸獄，囚既猥多，難於隔訊，盛夏疾疫，傳致瘐死，或主者異見，歲時不決，朕甚愍焉。

translations.literal: Now when metropolitan officials are impeached and tried, all are temporarily detained in Kaifeng's various prisons; prisoners being so numerous, separate interrogation is difficult; in midsummer epidemics spread, leading to death from illness in detention, or the presiding officials hold differing views and cases drag on year after year without decision—the emperor is deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Today impeached metropolitan officials are all held in Kaifeng's various prisons; with so many prisoners, separate interrogation is difficult; midsummer epidemics cause deaths in detention, or presiding officials disagree and cases linger unresolved for years—the emperor is deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 其復大理獄，置卿一人，少卿二人，丞四人，專主鞫訊；

translations.literal: Let the Court of Judicial Review prison be restored; appoint one chief, two vice chiefs, and four assistants, specializing in interrogation;
translations.idiomatic: Restore the Court of Judicial Review prison; appoint one chief, two vice chiefs, and four assistants devoted to interrogation;

sentences.zh: 檢法官二人，主簿一人。

translations.literal: two legal inspectors and one registrar.
translations.idiomatic: also appoint two legal inspectors and one registrar.

sentences.zh: 應三司、諸寺監吏犯杖、笞不俟追究者，聽即決，餘悉送大理獄。

translations.literal: For clerks of the Three Departments and various directorates and commissions guilty of bastinado or cudgel offenses not awaiting further investigation, immediate judgment is permitted; all others are sent to the Court of Judicial Review prison.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of the Three Departments and various directorates guilty of bastinado- or cudgel-level offenses not requiring further investigation may be judged on the spot; all others go to the Court of Judicial Review prison.

sentences.zh: 其應奏者，並令刑部、審刑院詳斷。

translations.literal: Those requiring submission shall all be carefully adjudicated by the Ministry of Justice and the Court for Review of Penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Cases requiring imperial submission shall be carefully adjudicated by the Ministry of Justice and the Court for Review of Penalties.

sentences.zh: 應天下奏按亦上之。」

translations.literal: All submitted cases from the realm shall also be sent upward."
translations.idiomatic: All submitted cases from across the realm shall also be forwarded to the court.

sentences.zh: 五年，分命少卿左斷刑 、右治獄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the vice chiefs were separately assigned: the left to adjudicate penalties, the right to manage the prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the vice chiefs were given separate duties: the left vice chief adjudicated penalties, the right managed the prison.

sentences.zh: 斷刑則評事、檢法詳斷，丞議，正審；

translations.literal: For adjudicating penalties, judicial reviewers and legal inspectors carefully adjudicated, assistants deliberated, and the chief gave final review;
translations.idiomatic: In penalty adjudication, judicial reviewers and legal inspectors decided cases, assistants deliberated, and the chief gave final review;

sentences.zh: 治獄則丞專推劾，主簿掌按籍，少卿分領其事，而卿總焉。

translations.literal: for managing the prison, assistants specialized in investigation and impeachment, the registrar kept the case register, the vice chiefs divided the duties, and the chief oversaw all.
translations.idiomatic: in prison management, assistants handled investigation and impeachment, the registrar kept the case register, the vice chiefs divided the work, and the chief oversaw all.

sentences.zh: 六年，刑部言：「舊詳斷官分公按訖，主判官論議改正，發詳議官覆議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ministry of Justice stated: "Formerly, after the detailed-review officials divided the public cases and finished, the presiding official deliberated and corrected them, and sent them to the deliberation officials for re-deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Ministry of Justice reported: "Formerly, after detailed-review officials finished dividing public cases, the presiding official deliberated and corrected them, then sent them to deliberation officials for re-deliberation.

sentences.zh: 有差失問難，則書於檢尾，送斷官改正，主判官審定，然後判成。

translations.literal: When there were errors and objections, they were written at the end of the review document, sent to the adjudicating officials for correction, the presiding official made final determination, and only then was judgment completed.
translations.idiomatic: When errors were found, notes were appended to the review document, sent back to adjudicating officials for correction, finalized by the presiding official, and only then was judgment completed.

sentences.zh: 自詳斷官歸大理為評事、司直，議官為丞，所斷按草，不由長貳，類多差忒。」

translations.literal: Since detailed-review officials returned to the Court of Judicial Review as judicial reviewers and case investigators, and deliberation officials became assistants, the draft judgments of cases adjudicated no longer passed through the chief and vice chiefs, and errors were frequent."
translations.idiomatic: After detailed-review officials returned to the Court of Judicial Review as judicial reviewers and case investigators, and deliberation officials became assistants, draft judgments no longer passed through the chief and vice chiefs, and errors became frequent.

sentences.zh: 迺定制：分評事、司直與正為斷司，丞與長貳為議司。

translations.literal: Thereupon regulations were fixed: judicial reviewers and case investigators together with the chief formed the Adjudication Division; assistants together with the chief and vice chiefs formed the Deliberation Division.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were then fixed: judicial reviewers and case investigators together with the chief formed the Adjudication Division; assistants with the chief and vice chiefs formed the Deliberation Division.

sentences.zh: 凡斷公按，正先詳其當否，論定則簽印注日，移議司覆議，有辨難，乃具議改正，長貳更加審定，然後判成錄奏。

translations.literal: For all adjudication of public cases, the chief first examined whether they were correct; once determination was settled he signed, sealed, and noted the date, and moved them to the Deliberation Division for re-deliberation; if there were objections, then deliberation with corrections was prepared, the chief and vice chiefs further made final determination, and only then was judgment completed, recorded, and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In all public cases the chief first reviewed correctness; once satisfied he signed, sealed, and dated the record and forwarded it to the Deliberation Division; if objections arose, revised deliberations were prepared, the chief and vice chiefs made final determination, and only then was judgment completed, recorded, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，三省言：「舊置糾察司，蓋欲察其違慢，所以謹重獄事，罷歸刑部，無復糾察之制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, the Three Departments stated: "Formerly the Inspectorate was established precisely to detect delay and negligence, thereby giving weight to prison affairs; after abolition and return to the Ministry of Justice, there was no longer an inspection system.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou the Three Departments reported: "The Inspectorate had been established precisely to detect delay and negligence in prison affairs; after its abolition and the return of duties to the Ministry of Justice, no inspection system remained.

sentences.zh: 請以糾察職事，委御史臺刑察兼之，臺獄則尚書省右司糾察之。」

translations.literal: We request that inspectorate duties be entrusted jointly to the Censorate's Penal Inspection section; Censorate prisons shall be inspected by the Right Office of the Ministry of Revenue in the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that inspectorate duties be assigned to the Censorate's Penal Inspection section; Censorate prisons shall be inspected by the Secretariat's Right Office of the Ministry of Revenue."

sentences.zh: 三年，罷大理寺獄。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Court of Judicial Review prison was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Court of Judicial Review prison was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，大理置獄，本以囚繫淹滯，俾獄事有所統，而大理卿崔台符等不能奉承德意，雖士大夫若命婦，獄辭小有連逮，輒捕繫。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Court of Judicial Review prison was established, it was precisely because prisoners were detained for long periods and prison affairs needed unified oversight; yet Chief Cui Taifu and others could not carry out the imperial intent—though gentry and wives of officials were involved, if prison testimony even slightly implicated them, they were promptly arrested and detained.
