translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Judicial Review prison was first established, the aim was to end prolonged detention and give prison affairs unified oversight; yet Chief Cui Taifu and others failed to carry out the imperial intent—even gentry and officials' wives were promptly arrested whenever prison testimony even slightly implicated them.

sentences.zh: 凡邏者所探報，即下之獄。

translations.literal: Whatever tip-off reports the censors submitted was immediately sent down to the prison.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever tip-offs the censors submitted went straight to the prison.

sentences.zh: 傅會鍛鍊，無不誣服。

translations.literal: Through fabrication and coerced confession, none failed to confess falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Through fabricated charges and coerced confessions, none failed to admit falsely.

sentences.zh: 至是，台符等皆得罪，獄迺罷。

translations.literal: At this point Taifu and the others all incurred guilt, and the prison was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu and his colleagues were all punished, and the prison was abolished.

sentences.zh: 八年，中書省言：「昨詔內外，歲終具諸獄囚死之數。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Secretariat stated: "Yesterday an edict ordered within and without that at year's end the number of prisoners who died in detention be reported.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Secretariat reported: "An edict recently ordered all jurisdictions to report at year's end the number of prisoners who died in detention.

sentences.zh: 而諸路所上，遂以禁繫二十而死一者不具，即是歲繫二百人，許以十人獄死，恐州縣弛意獄事，甚非欽恤之意。」

translations.literal: Yet what the circuits submitted omitted cases where one died among twenty detained—meaning that detaining two hundred for the year permitted ten prison deaths; we fear prefectures and counties will relax concern for prison affairs, which is very far from the intent of reverent compassion."
translations.idiomatic: Yet circuit reports omitted cases where one prisoner died among twenty detained—effectively allowing ten deaths per two hundred detainees per year; we fear prefectures and counties will neglect prison affairs, contrary to reverent compassion."

sentences.zh: 詔刑部自今不許輒分禁繫之數。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Justice that from now on dividing the number detained shall not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Justice that from now on no report may divide the total number detained.

sentences.zh: 紹聖二年，戶部如三司故事，置推勘檢法官，應在京諸司事干錢穀當追究者，從杖已下即定斷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng, the Ministry of Revenue, following the precedent of the Three Departments, established investigating and legal-inspection officials; for matters in metropolitan offices involving grain and funds requiring investigation, judgment up to and including the bastinado could be rendered immediately.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 2 (1095), the Ministry of Revenue, following Three Department precedent, established investigating and legal-inspection officials; for metropolitan cases involving grain and funds requiring investigation, judgment up to bastinado level could be rendered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 三年 ，復置大理寺右治獄，官屬視元豐員，仍增置司直一員。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Court of Judicial Review's right prison-management office was restored; its staff matched the Yuanfeng complement, with one additional case investigator added.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Court of Judicial Review's right prison-management office was restored; staffing matched the Yuanfeng complement, with one additional case investigator.

sentences.zh: 大理卿路昌衡請：「分大理寺丞為左、右推，若有 異，自左移右。

translations.literal: Chief Lu Changheng requested: "Divide the Court of Judicial Review assistants into left and right investigators; if there is disagreement, transfer from left to right.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Lu Changheng requested: "Court of Judicial Review assistants should be divided into left and right investigators; if they disagree, cases move from left to right.

sentences.zh: 再變，即命官審問，或御史臺推究。

translations.literal: If changed again, then appoint an official to conduct examination, or have the Censorate investigate.
translations.idiomatic: If disagreement persists, appoint an official to examine the case, or have the Censorate investigate.

sentences.zh: 不許開封府互勘及地分探報，庶革互送挾之弊。

translations.literal: Do not permit the Kaifeng prefectural office to conduct mutual investigation or local tip-off reports, so as to eliminate the abuse of passing cases back and forth for leverage.
translations.idiomatic: Do not allow the Kaifeng prefectural office to conduct mutual investigations or local tip-offs, so as to eliminate the abuse of shuffling cases for leverage.

sentences.zh: 徒已上罪，移御史臺。

translations.literal: Offenses of penal servitude and above are transferred to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses at penal servitude and above are transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 命官追攝者，悉依條。

translations.literal: When appointed officials are summoned for arrest, all follow the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When appointed officials are summoned for arrest, all procedures follow statute.

sentences.zh: 若探報涉虛、用情託者，並收坐以聞。」

translations.literal: If tip-off reports prove false or favoritism is employed, all involved shall be charged and reported."
translations.idiomatic: If tip-offs prove false or favoritism is shown, all involved shall be charged and reported."

sentences.zh: 初，法寺斷獄，大辟失入有罰，失出不坐。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Court of Judicial Review decided cases, wrongful conviction of a capital offense carried punishment, but wrongful acquittal carried none.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when the Court of Judicial Review decided cases, wrongful conviction in a capital case carried punishment, but wrongful acquittal did not.

sentences.zh: 至是，以失出死罪五人比失入一人，失出徒、流罪三名，亦如之。

translations.literal: At this point, five wrongful acquittals of a capital offense were treated as one wrongful conviction; three wrongful acquittals of penal servitude or exile offenses were treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Now five wrongful acquittals in capital cases were treated as one wrongful conviction; three wrongful acquittals in penal servitude or exile cases were treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: This was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This was enacted as a statute.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，刑部言：「祖宗重失入之罪，所以恤刑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu, the Ministry of Justice stated: "The founding emperors treated wrongful conviction as a grave offense, thereby showing compassion in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 3 (1100), the Ministry of Justice reported: "The founding emperors treated wrongful conviction as a grave offense, thereby showing compassion in the application of punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫失出，臣下之小過；

translations.literal: Now, excessive leniency in sentencing is a minor fault of officials;
translations.idiomatic: Excessive leniency in sentencing is, after all, only a minor fault on the part of officials;

sentences.zh: 好生，聖人之大德。

translations.literal: Cherishing life is the great virtue of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing life is the sage's supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 請罷失出之責，使有司讞議之間，務盡忠恕。」

translations.literal: We request that the penalty for excessive leniency be abolished, so that when responsible offices deliberate on cases, they may fully practice loyalty and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that liability for excessive leniency be abolished, so that in deliberating cases responsible offices may fully embody loyalty and humane forbearance.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，臣僚言：「遠方官吏，文法既疏，刑罰失中，不能無。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, a member of the bureaucracy said: "Officials in distant regions, since statutes and procedures are loosely applied and punishments often miss the mark, cannot be entirely without error.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenghe (1113), an official memorialized: "In the remote circuits, where legal standards are lax and punishments often miss the mark, wrongful outcomes cannot be entirely avoided.

sentences.zh: 願委耳目之官，季一分錄所部囚禁，遇有抑，先釋而後以聞。

translations.literal: We wish that supervisory officials—the eyes and ears of the throne—each quarter record one-tenth of the prisoners in their jurisdiction; when there is oppression, release them first and then report.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that supervisory officials, the court's eyes and ears, each quarter register one-tenth of the prisoners under their jurisdiction; whenever oppression is found, they should release the prisoner first and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 歲終較所釋多寡，為之殿最。

translations.literal: At year's end compare how many were released, and use this for ranking superior and inferior performance.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end the number released should be compared and used to rank officials as superior or inferior.

sentences.zh: 其徼功故出有罪者，論如法。」

translations.literal: Those who, seeking merit, deliberately release the guilty shall be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who, seeking credit, deliberately releases the guilty shall be prosecuted under the law.

sentences.zh: 詔令刑 部立法：「諸入人徒、流之罪已結案，而錄問官吏能駮正，或因事而能推正者，累及七人，比大辟一名推賞。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to legislate: "Whenever a case of penal servitude or exile already closed is overturned by the recording-and-interrogation official, or is corrected in the course of the matter, if seven persons are affected in total, reward as for one capital case."
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Ministry of Justice to draft regulations: "In any closed case of penal servitude or exile that a recording-and-interrogation official overturns, or that is corrected in the course of review, if seven persons are affected in all, the official shall receive the same commendation as for correcting one capital case."

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，令諸鞫勘有情款異同而病死者，提刑司研究之，如 ，申朝廷取旨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing, it was ordered that in all interrogations where the confessions differed and the prisoner died of illness, the Judicial Commissioner's office should investigate; if there was wrongful conviction, report to the court for decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shaoxing (1136), an order required that whenever an interrogation produced conflicting confessions and the prisoner died in custody, the circuit Judicial Commissioner should investigate; if a wrongful conviction was found, the case was to be reported to the throne for decision.

sentences.zh: 十二年，令諸推究翻異獄，毋差初官、蔭子及新進士，擇曾經歷任人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, it was ordered that in all reinvestigations of overturned cases, newly appointed officials, yin-privilege holders, and new jinshi degree holders were not to be assigned; choose men with prior experience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1142), an order stipulated that in reinvestigating overturned cases, newly appointed officials, holders of hereditary privilege, and fresh jinshi graduates were not to be assigned; experienced officials were to be selected instead.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，令監察御史每冬夏點獄，有鞫勘失實者，照刑部郎官，直行移送。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, it was ordered that investigating censors each winter and summer inspect the prisons; where interrogation had been false, follow the precedent for Ministry of Justice bureau directors and transfer directly for prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1157), investigating censors were ordered to inspect prisons every winter and summer; when an interrogation was found false, the responsible officials were to be transferred for prosecution under the same rules applied to directors in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，令殺人無證、屍不經驗之獄，具案奏裁，委提刑審問。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, it was ordered that in homicide cases without witnesses and where the corpse had not been examined, the full case was to be memorialized for imperial decision and entrusted to the Judicial Commissioner for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1159), cases of homicide lacking witnesses or without examination of the corpse were to be submitted in full for imperial decision and referred to the Judicial Commissioner for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 如有可疑及翻異，從本司差官重勘，案成上本路，移他監司審定，具案聞奏。

translations.literal: If there was cause for doubt or a confession was overturned, the office itself was to assign an official to reinvestigate; when the case was complete it was to be sent up within the circuit, transferred to another supervisory commissioner for review and determination, and the case reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: If doubt remained or a confession was overturned, the office was to assign an official to reinvestigate; once complete, the file went up within the circuit, was sent to another supervisory commissioner for review, and was then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 否則監司再遣官勘之，又不伏，復奏取旨。

translations.literal: Otherwise the supervisory commissioner again dispatched an official to investigate; if the prisoner still would not submit, the case was again memorialized for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the supervisory commissioner sent another investigator; if the prisoner still refused to accept the finding, the case was again submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 先是，有司建議：「外路獄三經翻異，在千里內者移大理寺。」

translations.literal: Earlier, responsible offices had proposed: "For cases in the outer circuits overturned three times, if within a thousand li, transfer to the Supreme Court."
translations.idiomatic: Previously officials had proposed: "For outer-circuit cases overturned three times, if within a thousand li, transfer them to the Supreme Court."

sentences.zh: 三十一年，刑部以為非祖宗法，遂釐正之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, the Ministry of Justice held that this was not the law of the founding ancestors and corrected it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1161), the Ministry of Justice ruled that this was not ancestral practice and rectified the rule.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，諸州翻異之囚，既經本州，次檄路，或再翻異，乃移隔路，至有越兩路者。

translations.literal: During the Qiandao era, prisoners who overturned their confessions, having already passed through their own prefecture, were next sent to the adjacent circuit; if they overturned again, the case was moved to a non-adjacent circuit, and there were even cases crossing two circuits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiandao period (1165–1173), prisoners who overturned their confessions, after review in their home prefecture, were next sent to the adjacent circuit; a second reversal could move the case to a distant circuit, and some cases even crossed two circuits.

sentences.zh: 官吏旁午於道，逮繫者困於追對。

translations.literal: Officials hurried back and forth on the roads, and those held in custody were worn down by repeated confrontations.
translations.idiomatic: Officials shuttled endlessly along the roads, while detainees were exhausted by repeated hearings.

sentences.zh: 四年，乃令：「鞫勘本路累嘗差官猶稱者，惟檄路，如尚翻異，則奏裁。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an order was issued: "In interrogations within the circuit where officials had repeatedly been assigned and the prisoner still maintained his claim, send only to the adjacent circuit; if he still overturned his confession, then memorialize for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1168), an order declared: "When a circuit had repeatedly assigned investigators and the prisoner still maintained his claim, the case went only to the adjacent circuit; if he overturned his confession again, it was submitted for imperial decision."

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年，令縣尉權縣事，毋自鞫獄，即令丞、簿參之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi, it was ordered that when a county captain temporarily held county affairs, he was not to interrogate cases himself, but was to have the county aide and registrar participate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunxi (1176), when a county captain temporarily administered a county, he was forbidden to interrogate cases himself; the county aide and registrar were to participate instead.

sentences.zh: 全闕，則於州官或縣選官權攝。

translations.literal: If both were absent, then a prefectural official or an official selected from a neighboring county was to serve temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: If both were unavailable, a prefectural official or an appointee from a neighboring county was to serve in their place.

sentences.zh: 金作贖刑 ，蓋以鞭扑之罪，情法有可議者，則寬之也。

translations.literal: Using gold to redeem punishment—this was for flogging offenses where circumstances and law admitted debate, and leniency was applied.
translations.idiomatic: "Using gold to redeem punishment" applied to flogging offenses where facts or law left room for argument, and clemency could be shown.

sentences.zh: 穆王贖及五刑，非法矣。

translations.literal: King Mu extended redemption to the five punishments—this was unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: When King Mu extended monetary redemption to all five punishments, he departed from proper law.

sentences.zh: 宋損益舊制，凡用官蔭得減贖，所以尊爵祿、養廉恥也。

translations.literal: The Song modified the old system: all who could use official yin privilege to reduce or redeem did so, thereby honoring rank and salary and nurturing integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: The Song adjusted the old system so that those entitled by official yin privilege could reduce or redeem penalties—honoring rank and emolument and cultivating a sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，大理正高繼申上言：「《刑統》名例律：三品、五品、七品以上官，親屬犯罪，各有等第減贖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, Senior Correcting Judge Gao Jishen memorialized: "The Statutes, General Principles: for officials of third, fifth, and seventh rank and above, when relatives commit crimes, each rank has its graduated reduction or redemption.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande (966), Senior Correcting Judge Gao Jishen memorialized: "The Statutes' General Principles provide that relatives of officials of third, fifth, and seventh rank and above receive graduated reductions or redemption according to rank.

sentences.zh: 恐年代已深，不肖自恃先蔭，不畏刑章。

translations.literal: I fear that as years have deepened, unworthy men rely on ancestral privilege and do not fear the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: As generations pass, I fear that unworthy men rely on ancestral privilege and no longer fear the penal code.

sentences.zh: 今犯罪身無官，須祖、父曾任本朝官，據品秩得減贖；

translations.literal: Now when the offender himself holds no office, his grandfather and father must have served as officials of this dynasty, and according to rank he may obtain reduction or redemption;
translations.idiomatic: When the offender himself holds no office, his grandfather or father must have served this dynasty; only then may he claim reduction or redemption according to their rank;

sentences.zh: 如仕于前代，須有功惠及民、為時所推、歷官三品以上，乃得請。」

translations.literal: if they served in a previous dynasty, they must have had meritorious benefit to the people, been esteemed in their time, and reached third rank or above—only then may one petition.
translations.idiomatic: if they served a prior dynasty, they must have benefited the people, won contemporary esteem, and reached third rank or above before a petition may be granted.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 後又定：「流內品官任流外職，準律文，徒罪以上依當贖法。

translations.literal: Later it was further fixed: "When a ranked official within the exile class holds an unranked post, follow the statutory text; for penal servitude and above apply the redemption-by-substitution law.
translations.idiomatic: Later a rule was added: "When a ranked official serving in an unranked post commits penal servitude or a greater offense, the statutory redemption-by-substitution rules apply.

sentences.zh: 諸司授勒留官及歸司人犯徒流等罪，公罪許贖，私罪以決罰論。」

translations.literal: When officials retained on assignment or returned personnel commit penal servitude, exile, or the like, public offenses may be redeemed; private offenses are punished by direct penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Officials retained on assignment or returned personnel who commit penal servitude or exile may redeem public offenses; private offenses are punished directly."

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，詔諸州民犯罪，或入金贖，長吏得以任情而輕重之，自今不得以贖論。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, an edict declared that when commoners in the various prefectures committed crimes, or paid gold to redeem punishment, the chief official might at discretion make it lighter or heavier; from now on redemption was not to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua (993), an edict ended the practice by which prefectural chiefs could arbitrarily lighten or aggravate monetary redemption when commoners paid to redeem punishment; henceforth such payments would not count as legal redemption.

sentences.zh: 婦人犯杖以下，非故為，量輕重笞罰或贖銅釋之。

translations.literal: When women committed beating with the staff or lesser offenses, if not deliberate, according to severity apply beating with the bamboo or release on payment of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Women convicted of staff-beating or lesser offenses, when the act was not deliberate, were to receive bamboo strokes according to severity or be released on payment of copper.

sentences.zh: 仁宗深憫夫民之無知也，欲立贖法以待薄刑，迺詔有司曰：「先王用法簡約，使人知禁而易從。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong deeply pitied the people's lack of understanding and wished to establish a redemption law to await lighter punishments; he then issued an edict the responsible offices, saying: "The former kings used law sparingly, so that people would know what was forbidden and easily comply.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved by the people's ignorance, Emperor Renzong wished to establish a redemption law for lesser penalties and issued an edict the responsible offices: "The ancient kings kept the law simple so people could know the prohibitions and obey them easily.

sentences.zh: 後代設茶、酒、鹽稅之禁，奪民厚利， 刑 用滋章。

translations.literal: Later ages established prohibitions on tea, wine, and salt tax, seizing the people's substantial profits, and the use of punishments grew ever more elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties imposed monopolies on tea, wine, and salt, seizing the people's livelihood, and punishments multiplied without end.

sentences.zh: 今之編敕，皆出律外，又數改更，官吏且不能曉，百姓安得聞之？

translations.literal: Today's compiled edicts all lie outside the code, and are repeatedly revised; even officials cannot understand them—how can the common people hear of them?
translations.idiomatic: Today's compiled edicts all exceed the basic code and are revised again and again; officials themselves can scarcely master them—how can common people even learn of them?

sentences.zh: 一陷于理，情雖可哀，法不得贖。

translations.literal: Once trapped in the law, though the circumstances are pitiable, the law does not permit redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Once caught in the net of law, however pitiable the circumstances, redemption is unavailable.

sentences.zh: 豈禮樂之化未行，而專用刑罰之弊與？

translations.literal: Is it that the transformation of rites and music has not been carried out, and the abuse of relying solely on punishments prevails?
translations.idiomatic: Has the civilizing force of rites and music failed, leaving us to rely on punishment alone?

sentences.zh: 漢文帝使天下人入粟於邊，以受爵免罪，幾于刑措。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han had the people of the realm contribute grain to the frontier to receive rank and remit crimes, and punishments nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han allowed people to send grain to the frontier in exchange for rank and remission of crimes, and executions nearly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 其議科條非著于律者，或冒利犯禁，奢侈違令，或過可憫，別為贖法。

translations.literal: The proposed articles not set down in the code—whether profiting by violation of prohibitions, extravagance contrary to edicts, or errors deserving pity—should have a separate redemption law.
translations.idiomatic: For offenses not codified in the statutes—profiteering against prohibitions, luxury in defiance of edicts, or blunders deserving pity—a separate redemption law should be created.

sentences.zh: 鄉民以穀麥，市人以錢帛，使民重穀麥，免刑罰，則農桑自勸，富壽可期矣。」

translations.literal: Country people with grain and wheat, townspeople with cash and silk—if the people value grain and wheat and are spared punishment, then farming and sericulture will encourage themselves, and wealth and long life may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Let villagers pay in grain and townspeople in cash and silk; if people value grain and are spared punishment, farming will flourish of itself and prosperity may follow.

sentences.zh: 詔下，論者以為富人得贖而貧者不能免，非朝廷用法之意。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, critics held that the rich could redeem while the poor could not escape, which was not the intent of the court in applying law.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, critics objected that the wealthy could buy their way out while the poor could not—contrary to the court's intent.

sentences.zh: 時命輔臣分總職事，以參知政事范仲淹領刑法，未及有所建明而仲淹罷，事遂寢。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers were assigned to oversee various duties; Vice Grand Councilor Fan Zhongyan took charge of criminal law, but before he could propose anything substantial Fan was dismissed and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers were then assigned portfolios; Vice Grand Councilor Fan Zhongyan oversaw criminal law, but before he could act he was dismissed and the plan lapsed.

sentences.zh: 至和初，又詔：「前代帝王後，嘗仕本朝官不及七品者，祖父母、父母、妻子罪流以下，聽贖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhihe, another edict declared: "Descendants of emperors of former dynasties who once served this dynasty in office below seventh rank—grandparents, parents, and wives, for offenses up to exile, may redeem.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhihe era (1054), another edict allowed redemption for grandparents, parents, and wives of descendants of former imperial houses who had served this dynasty below seventh rank, for offenses up to exile.

sentences.zh: 雖不仕而嘗被賜予者，有罪，非巨 ，亦如之。」

translations.literal: Even if they did not serve but once received imperial gifts, if guilty of offenses that are not extremely heinous, the same rule applies."
translations.idiomatic: Even those who never held office but had received imperial gifts might redeem, provided the offense was not extremely heinous."

sentences.zh: 隨州司理參軍李抃父毆人死，抃上所授官以贖父罪，帝哀而許之。

translations.literal: Li Bian, judicial assistant of Suizhou, whose father beat a man to death—Bian submitted the office he had received to redeem his father's crime; the emperor pitied him and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian, judicial assistant in Suizhou, whose father had beaten a man to death, offered his own appointment to redeem his father; the emperor, moved, consented.

sentences.zh: 君子謂之失刑 ，然自是未嘗為比。

translations.literal: Men of principle called this a lapse in justice, yet from then on it was never made a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle called it a failure of justice, yet it was never repeated.

sentences.zh: 而終宋之世，贖法惟及輕刑而已。

translations.literal: Throughout the Song, the redemption law extended only to lighter punishments.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of the dynasty, redemption applied only to lighter penalties.

sentences.zh: 恩宥之制，凡大赦及天下，釋雜犯死罪以下，甚則常赦所不原罪，皆除之。

translations.literal: The system of gracious pardon: for a general amnesty extending over the realm, release all mixed offenses below capital crime; in extreme cases even crimes normally excluded from regular amnesties were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the system of gracious pardon, a general amnesty covering the realm released all mixed offenses below capital crime; at its broadest, even offenses normally excluded from routine amnesties were cleared.

sentences.zh: 凡曲赦，惟一路或一州，或別京，或畿內。

translations.literal: For a partial amnesty, only one circuit, or one prefecture, or a separate capital, or the metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty applied to a single circuit, a single prefecture, a separate capital, or the metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 凡德音，則死及流罪降等，餘罪釋之，間亦釋流罪。

translations.literal: For a clemency edict, capital and exile offenses were reduced one grade; remaining offenses were released, and sometimes exile offenses were also released.
translations.idiomatic: A clemency edict reduced capital and exile sentences by one grade and released lesser offenses; exile was sometimes remitted as well.

sentences.zh: 所被廣狹無常。

translations.literal: The scope, broad or narrow, was not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Its scope—broad or narrow—was never fixed.

sentences.zh: 又，天子歲自錄京師繫囚，畿內則遣使，往往雜犯死罪以下，第降等，杖、笞釋之，或徒罪亦得釋。

translations.literal: Moreover, each year the Son of Heaven personally recorded prisoners in the capital; within the metropolitan region he dispatched envoys. Often for mixed offenses below capital crime they were merely reduced one grade, staff and bamboo offenses were released, or even penal servitude might be released.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the emperor personally reviewed prisoners in the capital; in the metropolitan region he sent envoys. Mixed offenses below capital crime were often reduced one grade; staff and bamboo punishments were remitted, and sometimes even penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 若?及諸路，則命監司錄焉。

translations.literal: If the review extended concurrently to the various circuits, supervisory commissioners were ordered to record them.
translations.idiomatic: When the review extended to the circuits as well, supervisory commissioners were ordered to register prisoners accordingly.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗因郊禮議赦，有秦再思者，上書願勿赦，引諸葛亮佐劉備數十年不赦事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Taizong was about to discuss amnesty on the occasion of the suburban sacrifice, Qin Zaisi memorialized asking that no amnesty be granted, citing Zhuge Liang's serving Liu Bei for decades without granting amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Emperor Taizong prepared to grant amnesty at the suburban sacrifice, Qin Zaisi petitioned against it, citing Zhuge Liang's decades of service under Liu Bei without ever proclaiming amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝頗疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 時趙普對曰：「凡郊祀肆眚，聖朝彝典，其仁如天，若劉備區區一方，臣所不取。」

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Pu replied: "Granting clemency at the suburban sacrifice is a constant institution of the sage dynasty; its benevolence is like Heaven. Liu Bei's petty corner of the realm—your servant will not take that as a model."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu replied: "Clemency at the suburban sacrifice is a sacred dynastic constant; its benevolence is heavenlike. Liu Bei's petty domain is no model for us."

sentences.zh: 上善之，遂定赦。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and fixed the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and confirmed the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖將祀南郊，詔：「兩京、諸道，自十月後犯強竊盜，不得預郊祀之赦。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Taizu was about to sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, an edict declared: "In the Two Capitals and all circuits, those who after the tenth month commit robbery or theft shall not participate in the suburban-sacrifice amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu prepared the Southern Suburb sacrifice, he issued an edict: "In both capitals and all circuits, robbery or theft committed after the tenth month shall not qualify for the suburban amnesty.

sentences.zh: 所在長吏告諭，民無冒法。」

translations.literal: Local chief officials were to announce and instruct the people so that none would violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Local chiefs were to proclaim the rule so that none would offend against it.

sentences.zh: 是後將祀，必先申明此詔。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever a sacrifice was imminent, this edict was first reasserted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, before each sacrifice, this restriction was reaffirmed.

sentences.zh: 天聖五年，馬亮言：「朝廷雖有是詔，而法官斷獄，乃言終是會赦，多所寬貸，惠姦失詔旨。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiansheng, Ma Liang said: "Although the court has this edict, when judges decide cases they say that in the end there will be amnesty and greatly lenient treatment, favoring the wicked and losing the intent of the edict."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiansheng (1027), Ma Liang said: "Though the court has this edict, judges still predict eventual amnesty and grant excessive leniency, indulging criminals and defeating the edict's purpose."

sentences.zh: 遂詔：「已下約束而犯劫盜，乃官典受贓，勿復奏，悉論如律。」

translations.literal: An edict followed: "Those who after this restriction commit robbery, or clerks who accept bribes, are not again to be memorialized; all are to be sentenced according to law."
translations.idiomatic: An edict responded: "Robbery after this deadline, or bribery by clerks, shall no longer be memorialized for special treatment; all such cases are to be sentenced by law."

sentences.zh: 七年春，京師雨，彌月不止。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, rain in the capital continued for a full month without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the seventh year (1029), rain in the capital fell without pause for a full month.

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂輔臣曰：「豈政事未當天心耶？」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said to his chief ministers: "Has governance failed to accord with Heaven's heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong asked his chief ministers: "Has our governance failed to accord with Heaven's will?"

sentences.zh: 因言：「向者大辟覆奏，州縣至於三，京師至於五，蓋重人命如此。

translations.literal: He then said: "Formerly, for capital cases submitted for review, prefectures and counties required three levels, the capital five—such was the weight placed on human life.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Formerly capital cases required three levels of review in the prefectures and counties, five in the capital—such was our regard for human life.

sentences.zh: 其戒有司，決獄議罪，毋或枉濫。」

translations.literal: Let this warn the responsible offices: in deciding cases and assessing guilt, do not act wrongly or excessively."
translations.idiomatic: Let this warn all who judge: decide cases and assess guilt without wrong or excess."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「赦不欲數，然捨是無以召和氣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "I do not wish amnesties to be frequent, yet apart from this there is no means to summon harmonious qi."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I do not wish amnesties to be frequent, yet without them there is no way to summon harmonious qi."

sentences.zh: 遂命赦天下。

translations.literal: He then ordered amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝在位久，明於人之情偽，尤惡訐人陰事，故一時士大夫習為惇厚。

translations.literal: The emperor reigned long and understood the truth and falsity in men's hearts; he especially hated those who denounced others' secret affairs, so for a time the scholar-officials practiced earnest sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reigned long, knew well the truth and falsity in men's hearts, and especially detested secret denunciation; for a time scholar-officials practiced sincere forbearance.

sentences.zh: 久之，小人乘間密上書，疏人過失，好事稍相與唱和，又按人赦前事。

translations.literal: After a long while, petty men seized the opportunity to submit secret memorials, laying bare others' faults; busybodies gradually joined in chorus, and again pressed matters from before amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In time petty men seized their chance with secret memorials exposing others' faults; busybodies took up the chorus and revived pre-amnesty grievances.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士張方平、御史呂誨以為言，因下詔曰：「蓋聞治古，君臣同心，上下協穆，而無激訐之俗，何其德之盛也！

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Zhang Fangping and Censor Lü Hui spoke on this, and an edict followed: "I have heard that in governing antiquity, ruler and ministers were of one mind, high and low harmonious, and there was no custom of fierce denunciation—how abundant was that virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Zhang Fangping and Censor Lü Hui remonstrated, prompting an edict: "In antiquity, ruler and ministers were united, high and low in harmony, and fierce denunciation had no place—what abundant virtue that was!

sentences.zh: 朕竊慕焉。

translations.literal: I secretly admire it.
translations.idiomatic: I aspire to it.

sentences.zh: 嘉與公卿大夫同底斯道，而教化未至，澆薄日滋。

translations.literal: I gladly share this way with the grand ministers, yet instruction has not arrived and shallow conduct daily increases.
translations.idiomatic: I would gladly walk this path with my ministers, yet instruction has not taken hold and shallow conduct grows daily.

sentences.zh: 比者中外羣臣，多上章言人過失，暴揚難驗之罪，或外託公言，內緣私忿，詆欺曖昧，苟陷善良。

translations.literal: Recently, inside and outside, many officials have memorialized others' faults, publicly airing charges hard to verify, or outwardly invoking public speech while inwardly following private resentment, slandering what is obscure, recklessly trapping the good.
translations.idiomatic: Lately officials at court and in the provinces have memorialized one another's faults, airing unverified charges, cloaking private grudges in public language, and slandering the innocent on vague pretexts.

sentences.zh: 又赦令者，所以與天下更始，而有司多舉按赦前之事，殆非信命令，重刑罰，使人洒心自新之意也。

translations.literal: Moreover, amnesty edicts are meant to give the realm a fresh start, yet responsible offices often investigate and prosecute matters before amnesty—hardly the intent of trusting commands, honoring punishments, and letting people cleanse their hearts and renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty edicts are meant to give the realm a fresh start, yet offices often prosecute pre-amnesty conduct—hardly the way to make commands trusted, punishments respected, and hearts renewed.

sentences.zh: 今有上言告人罪，言赦前事者，訊之。

translations.literal: Hereafter, whoever memorializes to accuse another of a crime by citing pre-amnesty matters shall be interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who accuses another by citing pre-amnesty conduct shall himself be interrogated.

sentences.zh: 至於言官，宜務大體，非事關朝政，自餘小過細故，勿須察舉。」

translations.literal: As for remonstrating officials, they should attend to the larger pattern; unless the matter concerns court governance, for the rest—minor faults and trivial details—do not investigate and report."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials should keep to the larger pattern; unless a matter touches court governance, minor faults and trivial details need not be investigated or reported."

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，又詔曰：「夫赦令，國之大恩，所以蕩滌瑕穢，納於自新之地，是以聖王重焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, another edict declared: "Amnesty edicts are the great grace of the state, meant to wash away stains and admit men to the place of self-renewal; therefore the sage kings valued them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign Emperor Shenzong issued an edict: "Amnesty is the state's greatest grace, washing away stains and opening the way to renewal; sage kings therefore treasured it.

sentences.zh: 中外臣僚多以赦前事捃摭吏民，興起獄訟，苟有詿誤，咸不自安，甚非持心近厚之義，使吾號令不信於天下。

translations.literal: Inside and outside, many officials gather pre-amnesty matters against clerks and commoners, raising lawsuits; if there is any error, all are ill at ease—this is far from the meaning of keeping the heart near to generosity, and makes Our commands untrusted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials inside and outside dredge up pre-amnesty conduct against clerks and commoners and raise lawsuits; at the slightest error all live in fear—far from generous intent, and Our commands lose credibility across the realm.

sentences.zh: 其內外言事、按察官，毋得依前舉劾，具按取旨，否則科違制之罪。

translations.literal: Memorializing officials and investigating censors inside and outside must not, as before, impeach; submit the case for decision, or else incur the offense of violating an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Memorializing officials and investigating censors must not, as before, impeach on such grounds; they shall submit cases for decision or face punishment for violating an edict.

sentences.zh: 御史臺覺察彈奏，法寺有此奏按，許舉駁以聞。」

translations.literal: The Censorate shall monitor and impeach; if the judiciary has such a submitted case, impeachment and rebuttal are permitted to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate shall monitor and impeach; if the judiciary receives such a case, rebuttal may be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 知諫院司馬光言曰：「按察之官，以赦前事興起獄訟，禁之誠為大善。

translations.literal: Sima Guang, of the Remonstrance Bureau, said: "For investigating censors to raise lawsuits from pre-amnesty matters— forbidding this is indeed a great good.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang of the Remonstrance Bureau said: "Forbidding investigating censors to raise lawsuits from pre-amnesty conduct is indeed a great good.

sentences.zh: 至於言事之官，事體稍異。

translations.literal: As for memorializing officials, the substance of the matter is somewhat different.
translations.idiomatic: For memorializing officials, however, the matter is somewhat different.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 御史之職，本以繩按百僚，糾擿隱伏。

translations.literal: The censor's duty is fundamentally to inspect and press all officials, exposing what is hidden.
translations.idiomatic: The censor's duty is to inspect all officials and expose what is hidden.

sentences.zh: 姦邪之狀，固非一日所為。

translations.literal: The conduct of the wicked is certainly not the work of a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked conduct is never the work of a single day.

sentences.zh: 國家素尚寬仁，數下赦令，或一歲之間至於再三，若赦前之事皆不得言，則其可言者無幾矣。

translations.literal: The state has long honored generous forbearance and repeatedly issued amnesty edicts—sometimes three or four times within a single year; if pre-amnesty matters may never be spoken of, then little remains that may be said.
translations.idiomatic: The state has long favored leniency and issues amnesties repeatedly—sometimes three or four in a year; if pre-amnesty conduct may never be reported, little would remain for censors to say.

sentences.zh: 萬一有姦邪之臣，朝廷不知，誤加進用，御史欲言則違今日之詔，若其不言，則陛下何從知之。

translations.literal: If by chance there is a wicked minister whom the court does not know and mistakenly promotes, the censor wishing to speak violates today's edict; if he does not speak, how is Your Majesty to know?
translations.idiomatic: Should a wicked minister escape notice and win promotion, a censor who speaks violates today's edict; if he stays silent, how will Your Majesty know?

sentences.zh: 臣恐因此言者得以藉口偷安，姦邪得以放心不懼。

translations.literal: I fear that thereby memorializers will seize an excuse for ease, and the wicked will be unafraid at heart.
translations.idiomatic: I fear memorializers will seize an excuse for complacency and the wicked will no longer fear exposure.

sentences.zh: 此乃人臣之至幸，非國家之長利也。

translations.literal: This is the utmost good fortune for ministers, not the lasting benefit of the state.
translations.idiomatic: That would be the officials' greatest comfort, not the state's lasting good.

sentences.zh: 請追改前詔，刊去『言事』兩字。」

translations.literal: I request that the previous edict be revised and the two characters 'memorializing officials' struck out.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the prior edict be revised and the words 'memorializing officials' removed.

sentences.zh: 光論至再，帝諭以「言者好以赦前事誣人」，光對曰：「若言之得實，誠所欲聞，若其不實，當罪言者。」

translations.literal: Guang argued twice; the emperor instructed him that "memorializers like to slander people with pre-amnesty matters." Guang replied: "If what they say is true, that is indeed what I wish to hear; if it is not true, the speaker should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Guang argued twice. The emperor said memorializers liked to slander people with pre-amnesty charges. Guang replied: "If true, that is exactly what I wish to hear; if false, punish the speaker."

sentences.zh: 帝命光送詔于中書。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guang to deliver the edict to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guang to take the edict to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年三月，帝以旱，欲降赦。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Xining, the emperor, because of drought, wished to grant amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year of Xining (1074), drought moved the emperor to grant amnesty.

sentences.zh: 時已兩赦，王安石曰：「湯旱，以六事自責曰：『政事不節與？』

translations.literal: There had already been two amnesties; Wang Anshi said: "When Tang faced drought, he blamed himself in six matters, saying: 'Was governance not disciplined?
translations.idiomatic: Two amnesties had already been issued. Wang Anshi said: "When the sage-king Tang faced drought, he blamed himself in six matters: 'Was my governance undisciplined?

sentences.zh: 若一歲三赦，是政不節矣，非所以弭災也。」

translations.literal: If there are three amnesties in one year, governance is undisciplined; this is not the way to quell disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: Three amnesties in one year mean undisciplined governance; that is no way to end a disaster."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 八年，編定廢免人敘格，常赦則郡縣以格敘用，凡三朞一敘，即朞未滿而遇非次赦者，亦如之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the regulations for reinstatement of dismissed persons were compiled; on regular amnesty the prefectures and counties reinstated according to the schedule—generally one reinstatement every three periods; if a period was not complete and a special amnesty occurred, the same rule applied.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1075), regulations for reinstating dismissed officials were compiled; on routine amnesty prefectures and counties reinstated by schedule—generally one reinstatement every three periods; if a special amnesty came before a period ended, the same rule applied.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，門下省言：「當官以職事墮曠，雖去官不免，猶可言；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, the Gate Department said: "When an official is negligent in duty, though he leaves office he is not exempt and may still be prosecuted;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou (1086), the Gate Department said: "Negligence in office may still be prosecuted after an official leaves his post;

sentences.zh: 至於赦降大恩，與物更始，雖劫盜殺人亦蒙寬宥，豈可以一事差失，負罪終身？

translations.literal: but when amnesty descends as a great grace and all things begin anew, even robbery and homicide receive leniency—how can one error make guilt lifelong?
translations.idiomatic: but when amnesty descends as a great grace and all things begin anew, even robbery and homicide receive mercy—how can a single lapse burden one for life?

sentences.zh: 今刑部所修不以去官、赦降原減條 ，請更刪改。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice is now compiling provisions that do not remit or reduce on account of leaving office or amnesty; we request further deletion and revision."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice is now drafting provisions that withhold remission or reduction after leaving office or under amnesty; we request that these be revised or deleted."

sentences.zh: 徽宗在位二十五年，而大赦二十六，曲赦十四，德音三十七。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong reigned twenty-five years, yet granted twenty-six general amnesties, fourteen partial amnesties, and thirty-seven clemency edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong reigned twenty-five years yet proclaimed twenty-six general amnesties, fourteen partial amnesties, and thirty-seven clemency edicts.

sentences.zh: 而南渡之後，紹熙歲至四赦，蓋刑政紊而恩益濫矣。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, in the Shaoxi years amnesty came four times a year—punishments grew disorderly and grace ever more excessive.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward retreat, the Shaoxi years saw amnesty as often as four times a year—criminal administration grew chaotic and clemency ever more excessive.

sentences.zh: 宋自祖宗以來，三歲遇郊則赦，此常制也。

translations.literal: From the founding ancestors onward, every three years when the suburban sacrifice occurred there was amnesty—this was the regular institution.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding ancestors onward, amnesty accompanied the suburban sacrifice every three years—this was regular practice.

sentences.zh: 世謂三歲一赦，於古無有。

translations.literal: The age calls it amnesty every three years; in antiquity there was nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: People say amnesty comes every three years; antiquity knew nothing like it.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，言者以為：「三王歲祀圜丘，未嘗輒赦。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era, memorializers held that: "The Three Sage-Kings each year sacrificed at the Round Mound and never casually granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyou era (1034–1038), critics argued: "The ancient sage-kings sacrificed yearly at the Round Mound and never casually granted amnesty.

sentences.zh: 自唐興兵以後，事天之禮不常行，因有大赦，以蕩亂獄。

translations.literal: From the Tang onward, after warfare arose, the rite of serving Heaven was not regularly performed, and therefore there were great amnesties to clear chaotic prisons.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang, when warfare disrupted regular worship of Heaven, great amnesties were used to empty overcrowded prisons.

sentences.zh: 且有罪者寬之未必自新，被害者抑之未必無怨。

translations.literal: Moreover, the guilty, when pardoned, do not necessarily reform; the injured, when suppressed, do not necessarily lack resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the guilty, when pardoned, do not necessarily reform; victims, when denied justice, do not necessarily cease to resent.

sentences.zh: 不能自新，將復為惡，不能無怨，將悔為善。

translations.literal: If they do not reform, they will again do evil; if they cannot cease to resent, they will regret having done good.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fail to reform will offend again; those who cannot cease to resent will regret having done good.

sentences.zh: 一赦而使民悔善長惡，政教之大患也。

translations.literal: One amnesty that makes the people regret doing good and nourish evil is a great calamity of government and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty that teaches people to regret virtue and nourish vice is a grave calamity for government and moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 願罷三歲一赦，使良民懷惠，凶人知禁。

translations.literal: We wish to abolish amnesty every three years, so that good people feel grace and wicked people know restraint.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to abolish the triennial amnesty, so the law-abiding feel protected and the wicked know restraint.

sentences.zh: 或謂未可盡廢，即請命有司，前郊三日理罪人，有過誤者引而赦之。

translations.literal: Some say it cannot be wholly abolished; then order the responsible offices that three days before the suburban sacrifice they review criminals, and those with errors release and amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Some say it cannot be abolished entirely; then let responsible offices, three days before the suburban sacrifice, review prisoners and release those whose offenses were mere error.

sentences.zh: 州縣須詔到倣此。」

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, when the edict arrives, should follow this model.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties should follow the same practice when the edict arrives.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，朝廷重其事，第詔：「罪人情重者，毋得以一赦免。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the court treated the matter seriously but issued only an edict: "Where the culprit's circumstances are grave, he must not be released by a single amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: The court took the memorial seriously but issued only an edict: "Where the offender's circumstances are grave, a single amnesty must not suffice for release.

sentences.zh: 然亦未嘗行。

translations.literal: Yet this too was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Even this was never enforced.
